operations.description:
Registers a new customer account on the shoppingMall platform. This operation creates a customer record with pending verification status, allowing temporary access to browse products but preventing order placement until email verification is completed.

The customer account is created with required fields: email, password_hash, first_name, last_name, created_at, and updated_at. The status is initialized as 'pending_verification' as specified in the shopping_mall_customers schema. The password_hash is stored using BCrypt algorithm for security, as required for authentication.

The operation requires the customer to provide valid, non-empty values for all required fields. The email must be unique across all actors, as enforced by the unique index on the email field. Subsequent API operations such as login and refresh will require a verified account with status 'active'.

After successful registration, an email verification notification is triggered automatically. The customer must click the verification link in the email to change their status from 'pending_verification' to 'active'. This security measure prevents unauthorized account creation using fake email addresses.

Related operations: GET /auth/customer/verify and POST /auth/customer/refresh. The verification endpoint must be called before attempting to use the login or refresh operations.

parameters.name: email
parameters.description: Customer's email address used for authentication and notifications. Must be unique across all actors and follow standard email format.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: Plain text password provided during registration. This will be hashed using BCrypt algorithm before storage in the password_hash field.

parameters.name: firstName
parameters.description: Customer's first/legal name as provided during registration. Required field with minimum length of 1 character.

parameters.name: lastName
parameters.description: Customer's last/legal name as provided during registration. Required field with minimum length of 1 character.

requestBody.description: Request body for customer account registration.

responseBody.description: Response containing authentication tokens and customer information after successful registration.

operations.name: join

operations.description:
Authenticates a customer's credentials and issues new access and refresh tokens. This operation validates the provided email and password against the stored password_hash in the shopping_mall_customers table.

The customer must have an 'active' status to successfully authenticate. Accounts with 'pending_verification' or 'suspended' status will be rejected. The operation checks the email address against the unique index on the email field in the customer table and verifies the password using BCrypt hashing algorithm.

After successful authentication, the system issues a short-lived access token and a refresh token stored securely in the customer_session record. The updated_at field in the shopping_mall_customers table is updated to reflect the last login time, which is used for activity monitoring and session management.

This operation does not support multiple concurrent sessions per device. If a customer logs in from a new device, the previous session's refresh token will be invalidated for security.

Related operations: POST /auth/customer/join, POST /auth/customer/refresh, and GET /auth/customer/logout. The join operation must be completed successfully before login, and refresh is used to extend the access token without requiring credentials again.

parameters.name: email
parameters.description: Customer's email address registered on the shoppingMall platform. Must match a unique email in the shopping_mall_customers table.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: Plain text password matching the BCrypt-hashed password_hash stored in the customer's record.

requestBody.description: Request body for customer authentication with email and password.

responseBody.description: Response containing successfully issued access and refresh tokens for the authenticated customer.

operations.name: login

operations.description:
Extends the validity of the customer's access token by exchanging a valid refresh token for new access and refresh tokens. This operation is used when the current access token has expired but the refresh token is still valid.

The refresh token must be present and valid in the customer_session record associated with the customer's account. The system validates the refresh token against the stored token in the customer_session table and checks that the corresponding customer account has 'active' status. If the customer is suspended or deleted, the refresh will be denied.

This process updates the refresh_token field in the customer_session record and resets the expiration timestamp for both the access and refresh tokens. The operation does not change the customer's authentication status or verify credentials again.

This operation is essential for maintaining a seamless user experience without requiring re-authentication for every API call. The access token typically expires after 15 minutes while the refresh token remains valid for up to 7 days.

Related operations: POST /auth/customer/join, POST /auth/customer/login, and GET /auth/customer/logout. Exchange is used after login or previous refresh operation, and must be called before the access token expires to maintain continuous session.

requestBody.description: Request body for token refresh using a valid refresh token.

responseBody.description: Response containing newly issued access and refresh tokens to extend the customer's session.

operations.name: refresh

operations.description:
Register a new seller account on the shoppingMall platform. This operation creates a seller record with initial status 'pending_verification'. The seller must provide a unique business email and secure password, which are stored in the email and password_hash fields respectively. The account is initially suspended until an admin reviews the submitted business information including business_name, business_address, and tax_id. The created_at timestamp records the registration time, and deleted_at remains null indicating the account is active but unverified. This operation is public and does not require authentication.

Security considerations require password hashing using BCrypt algorithm as specified in the schema. The email must be unique across the entire system as enforced by the unique index on the email field. This operation creates a foundational identity for the seller who will subsequently manage products, inventory, and customer orders.

The seller account is linked to the shopping_mall_seller_sessions table for session management and to shopping_mall_products for product listings. Upon successful registration, a temporary access token is issued for verification purposes. If the account remains unverified, it may be auto-deleted after 30 days as per platform policy.

This operation must be completed before the seller can upload products or access their storefront. The verification process requires submission of supporting documents and may take 1-3 business days.

No related API operations are required as prerequisites since this is the initial entry point for seller onboarding.

requestBody.description: Payload containing seller registration details.

responseBody.description: Contains authentication token and seller identity information upon successful registration.

operations.name: join

operations.description:
Authenticate an existing seller account using email and password credentials. This operation validates the email and password_hash values against the seller database record. When successful, the authentication system verifies the account status is 'active' and deleted_at is null, ensuring the seller account is not suspended or deactivated. The password must be verified using BCrypt protocol as established in the schema.

The authentication system enforces rate limiting on login attempts to prevent brute force attacks. Each successful login creates a corresponding record in the shopping_mall_seller_sessions table to track active sessions. The login operation returns a refresh token that can be used to obtain new access tokens without re-entering credentials.

This operation is crucial for granting sellers access to their management dashboard where they can perform product listing, order processing, and sales analytics. Before login, the seller must have completed the registration process and received admin approval, as indicated by a status value of 'active'.

Login attempts with invalid credentials are logged in the shopping_mall_access_logs table for security auditing. Multiple failed attempts trigger account lockout mechanisms. This operation has no prerequisites since it is the primary authentication entry point for sellers.

requestBody.description: Request body containing the seller's email and password for authentication.

responseBody.description: Returns JWT tokens for authenticated access to seller services. Includes refresh token for token renewal.

operations.name: login

operations.description:
Renew access to seller services using a valid refresh token without requiring email and password re-entry. This operation validates the refresh token against the shopping_mall_seller_sessions table to confirm the session is active and authenticated. Upon validation, a new access token is issued with a fresh lifecycle while maintaining the same seller identity.

The refresh token has a longer expiration period than the access token and must be stored securely by the client application. This operation ensures continuous access to seller management features without forcing frequent re-authentication, which would disrupt business operations like order fulfillment, inventory management, and customer communication.

The refresh operation does not change the seller's account status, which must remain 'active' with deleted_at = null for continued service. The refresh token is invalidated if the seller changes their password, their account is suspended by an admin, or if the session expires.

This operation is essential for maintaining uninterrupted seller experience across multiple devices and sessions. It follows the OAuth 2.0 refresh token pattern and complements the login operation. This operation has no prerequisites as it is designed to work independently after initial authentication.

requestBody.description: Contains the refresh token obtained during the login operation.

responseBody.description: Returns newly issued JWT access token for continued seller access to services.

operations.name: refresh

operations.description:
Registers a new admin account for platform administrators. This operation creates a new administrative identity with the provided email and password hash, initializing system access for privileged operations. The operation requires email validation through an out-of-band process, as admin accounts are manually created through secure internal procedures and cannot be self-registered publicly. The account begins in 'pending_verification' status until manually approved by an existing admin through the administrative console, after which status transitions to 'active'. All admin accounts must have a unique email, enforced by the unique index on shopping_mall_admins.email field. The password_hash field is stored as a BCrypt hash, never in plain text, as required by security protocols referenced in the security_and_compliance.md requirements document. When a new admin is created, the system automatically logs this event in the shopping_mall_audit_logs table for compliance tracking. This operation should be triggered by platform administrators through secure HR onboarding systems, not through public API endpoints.

Security considerations: This is a privileged operation requiring human approval and secure channel verification. Access to this endpoint is restricted to internal systems with physical and network security controls.

Relationship: This operation directly creates records in the shopping_mall_admins table. The account's status will be initialized as 'pending_verification' and must be manually upgraded to 'active' by an existing admin.

Related operations: Once the account is active, the admin can use the /auth/admin/login operation to authenticate.

requestBody.description: Registration parameters for creating a new admin account.

responseBody.description: The newly created admin entity with its assigned ID and initial status.

operations.name: join

operations.description:
Authenticates an admin user by verifying their email and password against the system database. This operation checks the provided email against the unique index on shopping_mall_admins.email field and validates the BCrypt-hashed password against the stored password_hash value. If authentication is successful, the user's status field must be 'active' to proceed; accounts with 'suspended' or 'pending_verification' status are denied access. On successful authentication, a new session record is created in the shopping_mall_admin_sessions table with the client's IP address, referrer URL, and href details. The session expires according to the platform's security policy (typically 8 hours of inactivity). The operation returns a refresh token and access token that are cryptographically signed and valid for subsequent API calls.

Security considerations: All login attempts are logged in the shopping_mall_access_logs table for audit purposes. Multiple failed attempts within 10 minutes trigger account lockout for 15 minutes, as defined by the security_and_compliance.md requirements. This operation requires secure HTTPS transmission and does not allow requests from untrusted domains.

Relationship: This operation reads from shopping_mall_admins table and creates records in shopping_mall_admin_sessions table. The operation is restricted to admin actors only.

Related operations: After successful login, admins can use the refresh operation to renew their access token, and the logout operation (if implemented) to terminate the session.

requestBody.description: Authentication parameters for admin login.

responseBody.description: Access and refresh tokens for authenticated admin session.

operations.name: login

operations.description:
Renews the access token for an authenticated admin session using a valid refresh token. This operation validates the refresh token against the system's token store, verifies that the associated shopping_mall_admin_sessions record is still active (expired_at is null), and checks that the admin account status is active. Upon validation, a new access token and refresh token pair are generated, extending the session duration according to the session timeout policy. The existing refresh token is invalidated and replaced with a new one following best practices for token rotation. The operation logs the refresh event in the shopping_mall_access_logs table for audit trail purposes.

Security considerations: Refresh tokens must be stored securely and should never be transmitted over insecure channels. Refresh token rotation prevents replay attacks and mitigates token theft risks. After successful token refresh, a new session record is created while the old one is marked for cleanup. This operation has an additional security layer requiring MFA validation if the user has configured it in their preferences, as referenced in the Authentication_Requirements.md document.

Relationship: This operation validates against shopping_mall_admin_sessions and shopping_mall_admins tables. It does not directly modify user data but updates authentication session state.

Related operations: This operation typically follows login. Once the access token expires, it's the only way to continue the session without re-authenticating with credentials.

requestBody.description: Refresh token for extending authenticated session.

responseBody.description: New access and refresh token pair for extended session.

Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of shopping mall customer accounts from the system. This operation operates on the shopping_mall_customers table and supports advanced search capabilities for finding customers based on multiple criteria including partial name matching, email domain filtering, registration date ranges, and account status.

The operation supports comprehensive pagination with configurable page sizes and sorting options. Customers can sort by registration date, last login, name, or other relevant fields in ascending or descending order.

Security considerations include rate limiting for search operations and appropriate filtering of sensitive customer information based on the requesting user's authorization level. Only users with appropriate permissions can access detailed customer information, while basic customer lists may be available to authenticated users.

This operation integrates with the shopping_mall_customers table as defined in the Prisma schema, incorporating all available customer fields and relationships. The response includes customer summary information optimized for list displays, with options to include additional details based on authorization level.

Retrieve detailed information about a specific shopping mall customer account by its unique identifier.

This operation fetches the complete customer profile from the shopping_mall_customers table, including personal information, account status, and registration metadata. The customer record returned is the full detail representation without summary reductions.

The operation validates that the requested customer exists and is not marked for deletion. If the customer is suspended, only limited public metadata is returned, while active customers return full profile details according to visibility rules.

Customer IDs are expected as UUIDs and must match the primary key format used in the shopping_mall_customers table. Endpoint access is public for customer self-lookup or restricted to administrators based on authorization settings.

Security: Rate limiting applies to prevent brute force attacks on customer identifiers. The response includes only information the requesting user has permission to view, with sensitive fields like password_hash always excluded.

Create a new customer account on the shoppingMall platform.

This operation allows a new user to register as a customer by providing their personal information and contact details. The system validates the email address format, checks for duplicate email accounts, and initiates a verification process to confirm ownership of the email address.

The operation creates a new record in the shopping_mall_customers table with initial status set to 'pending_verification'. The customer receives a verification email with a link that must be clicked to activate the account. Until verification is completed, the customer cannot access most platform features.

Security measures include password strength requirements, bcrypt password hashing, and rate limiting to prevent brute force attacks. The operation automatically generates a unique customer ID and timestamps for creation and update.

After successful creation, a JSON response returns the new customer record with a subset of fields for security reasons, excluding sensitive information like password_hash.

Related operations: GET /actors/customers/{customerId} to retrieve the verified customer details, PATCH /actors/customers to list all customers with pagination, and PUT /actors/customers/{customerId} to update customer information.

responseBody.description: The newly created customer account information, excluding sensitive data for security.

operations.description:
Update an existing customer's profile information on the shoppingMall platform.

This operation allows an authenticated customer to modify their personal details such as name, email, or contact preferences. The customer must be logged in and the operation validates that the requester matches the customerId in the path parameter.

The system ensures that email changes require verification, preventing unauthorized email takeover attempts. When the email is updated, the system marks the new email as pending verification and sends a verification email to the new address. Until confirmed, the customer can still use the platform with their original email.

The update operation only allows modification of fields permitted to customers: first_name, last_name, and notification preferences. Sensitive fields like password_hash are not modifiable directly through this endpoint - password changes must use the dedicated credential update workflow.

The operation modifies the existing customer record in the shopping_mall_customers table and updates the updated_at timestamp. The original status (active, suspended, pending_verification) is maintained unless explicitly changed through administrative processes.

For security and compliance reasons, the response returns the updated customer record in the same format as the create operation, excluding password_hash and other sensitive fields.

Related operations: POST /actors/customers to create new customer accounts, GET /actors/customers/{customerId} to retrieve customer details, and DELETE /actors/customers/{customerId} to suspend customer accounts.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the customer account to be updated. This must match the authenticated user's ID for security purposes.

responseBody.description: The updated customer account information, excluding sensitive data for security.

operations.description:
Permanently remove a customer account from the shoppingMall platform.

This operation deletes the customer record from the shopping_mall_customers table. The deletion is permanent and cannot be undone. All associated data including cart items, wishlists, order history, reviews, and loyalty points will be persistently removed from the database.

Security: Only authenticated administrators with 'admin' privileges can perform this operation.

Compliance: This hard delete operation is permitted only when required by legal or regulatory obligations, or when requested by the customer for data erasure under privacy regulations (e.g., GDPR Right to Erasure). The operation will trigger audit logging of the deletion event.

Relationships: This affects the following related entities that will also be permanently removed:
- shopping_mall_customer_sessions (all sessions)
- shopping_mall_carts (all active carts)
- shopping_mall_cart_items (all cart items)
- shopping_mall_wishlists (all wishlists)
- shopping_mall_wishlist_items (all wishlist items)
- shopping_mall_orders (all orders)
- shopping_mall_order_items (all order items)
- shopping_mall_order_payments (all payments)
- shopping_mall_order_shipping (all shipping information)
- shopping_mall_order_returns (all return requests)
- shopping_mall_reviews (all reviews)
- shopping_mall_review_images (all review images)
- shopping_mall_review_reactions (all reactions)
- shopping_mall_loyalty_points (all loyalty points balance)
- shopping_mall_loyalty_point_transactions (all transaction history)
- shopping_mall_notification_preferences (all notification preferences)
- shopping_mall_alerter_preferences (all alert preferences)

All DELETE operations on the shopping_mall_customers table are hard deletes with no soft-delete flag. The previous soft-delete mechanism has been removed for compliance with data minimization requirements in the platform's privacy policy.

parameters.name: customerId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target customer to be permanently deleted. This UUID references the id field in the shopping_mall_customers table.

Response includes the complete seller profile information including business_name, email, tax_id, business_address, status, created_at, and updated_at fields.

All seller records are filtered to exclude any records with deleted_at populated (already deleted sellers).

Security: This operation requires authentication as a platform admin user, but the results include all seller records regardless of admin permissions level.

This is a read-only operation that does not modify any data in the database. For creating or updating seller records, use the POST and PUT operations respectively.

This operation accepts the core seller registration data including business name, legal address, tax identification, and contact email. The password is encrypted using BCrypt upon creation and stored securely. Upon successful creation, the seller account enters a 'pending_verification' status and requires document submission for final approval.

The operation is only accessible via the seller registration interface and cannot be performed by administrators or other actors.

For security and compliance, this operation does not update sensitive authentication fields like email or password_hash, which are managed through separate secure workflows. The operation validates that the seller account exists and is not already deleted. If the status is changed to 'rejected' or 'suspended', all associated product listings are automatically deactivated and customers are notified of the change. The updated_at timestamp is automatically set by the system to record when the modification occurred. When status changes from 'pending_verification' to 'active', the system triggers background processes to validate tax documents and initialize the seller's storefront. This operation is governed by audit logs that record who made the changes and when, ensuring full compliance with financial and e-commerce regulations.

Note: This operation should only be used by admins for manual account management. Seller self-updates occur through the separate frontend profile management flow.

operations.description:
Permanently remove a seller account from the shoppingMall system. Unlike soft-deletion implemented through the deleted_at field, this operation performs a hard delete that removes the seller's entire record from the database. This should only be invoked under extreme compliance circumstances, such as verified fraudulent activity, legal court orders for data removal, or when a seller has been permanently revoked and all associated data has been archived or transferred according to regulatory requirements.

When this operation is executed, the system will:
- Delete the seller's record from the shopping_mall_sellers table
- Remove all associated seller session records from shopping_mall_seller_sessions
- Purge all seller-specified integration keys and credentials
- Archive related audit logs in a secure archival system rather than permanently deleting them

This hard delete affects several related entities including payment methods, coupons issued by this seller, and loyalty points associated with this seller's account. The operation is irreversible and cannot be undone.

Due to the irreversible nature of this operation, it is subject to multi-factor administrative approval. The caller must have direct 'admin' privileges, and an additional manual review by a senior compliance officer is required before execution.

This hard delete operation is exceptionally rare and should only occur after careful review of the financial and legal implications. The standard process for deactivating problematic sellers is to set status: 'rejected' or 'suspended' using the PUT /actors/sellers/{sellerId} operation instead.

Related operations: PUT /actors/sellers/{sellerId} - to suspend or reject a seller without permanent deletion.

IMPORTANT: Hard delete of any record is a compliance-critical action reserved for extreme situations only. This operation does NOT use the soft_delete_column convention and instead performs a direct database deletion of the entire row.

NOTE: This operation is fundamentally different from setting deleted_at to a date, which is the standard soft-delete mechanism used by the system for almost all records.

Create a new platform administrator account with elevated privileges for managing the shoppingMall platform.

This operation allows the creation of new admin accounts, which are required to perform administrative tasks such as approving/rejecting seller registrations, moderating content, managing user accounts, and accessing system-wide reports.

Administrative accounts are created manually through internal processes and are not accessible to regular users. The system enforces strict security requirements including mandatory multi-factor authentication (MFA) and encrypted password storage.

The operation validates that the admin email is unique across all actor types and follows the platform's email format requirements. Passwords must meet minimum security requirements of 12 characters with mixed case, numbers, and symbols.

Upon successful creation, the system automatically sends a secure onboarding email with instructions for setting up MFA. The admin account is initially created in 'pending_verification' status until the new admin completes the MFA setup process.

operations.description:
Permanently remove an administrative account from the shoppingMall platform.

This operation executes a hard delete of an admin record in the shopping_mall_admins table. The admin's account is completely removed from the system with no possibility of recovery. All associated session records and audit trails are also purged from the database.

Security considerations: This operation requires admin-level authorization. Only an authenticated admin user with elevated privileges can delete another admin account. This operation bypasses all soft-delete protections and cannot be reversed. After successful deletion, the admin's email becomes available for new registrations. This operation should only be used in cases of permanent account termination.

Implementation details: This operation directly removes the record from the shopping_mall_admins table in the database. Unlike other entities that use soft-deletion (deleted_at timestamp), admin accounts are subject to hard deletion for security and compliance reasons.

Related operations: This operation is an exception to the platform's usual soft-delete policy. The GET /actors/admins/{adminId} operation cannot retrieve any data after this delete operation has been executed, as the record is permanently removed.

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered, sorted, and paginated list of all products in the shoppingMall platform.

This operation performs a complex search across the shopping_mall_products table to return products based on dynamic criteria. It supports advanced filtering by status, price range, category, seller, and search keywords. Results are sorted by relevance, price, rating, or creation date and returned in paginated form with configurable page size.

The operation matches products by partial name match, category similarity, and seller association. It excludes archived products unless specifically requested. Products are ordered by a combination of sales volume, popularity, and freshness.

Security considerations: This is a public endpoint available to all users, including unauthenticated guests. Product visibility is determined by product status (published, archived) rather than user authentication. The operation does not expose sensitive product data like seller contact information or inventory levels.

Implementation details: This endpoint uses a composite query that joins shopping_mall_products with shopping_mall_categories and shopping_mall_sellers tables to enrich results with category names and seller names. The search algorithm prioritizes exact name matches over partial matches and considers product rating and sales history in relevance scoring. It has a maximum limit of 100 results per page and supports cursor-based pagination.

Related operations: POST /products creates a new product (requires seller authentication), PATCH /products/{productId} retrieves a specific product by ID, and GET /products/{productId}/reviews retrieves product reviews.

Performance considerations: This operation is optimized for handling datasets up to 100,000 products and returns results within 500ms under normal load conditions. Aggregation operations are performed using database-level indexing on status, price, and created_at fields.

This operation fetches a single product entity identified by its unique identifier, returning all available product details including title, description, price, tax category, and associated images. The product data comes from the shopping_mall_products Prisma model and is optimized for display in product detail pages.

Security: The operation is publicly accessible - any user can view product details. Product visibility is determined by its status field ('published') in the database, where only published products are returned. Archived or drafted products will return a 404 error.

The response includes a complete product object with all textual and numeric fields from the shopping_mall_products table, including created_at and updated_at timestamps. Product status is included to inform clients about availability.

Associated data: The product's primary image is included in the response as a full URL to the image file. This reference comes from the shopping_mall_product_images table, where the is_primary flag is used to identify the main product image. Related data from other tables (categories, tags, variants) is not included in this response for performance optimization.

Related operations: The GET /products endpoint provides a list of products in summary format. The PATCH /products endpoint allows searching products with filters.

Performance: This operation returns data from a single database record with a single join to product_images. Database queries are optimized with indexes on id and status fields to ensure sub-100ms response times even at high traffic volumes.

Error handling: Returns 404 Not Found if no product exists with the provided ID or if the product status is not 'published'.

operations.description:
Create a new product listing in the shoppingMall marketplace.

This operation allows authenticated sellers to create new product offerings for sale. The seller's identity is automatically extracted from the JWT authentication token and associated with the new product record. A product can only be created by a seller with active status ('active'), and the product's status is initially set to 'draft' to allow for review before publishing.

The product creation process requires: a title (3-100 characters), a description (minimum 20 characters), a price (minimum $0.01, maximum $5000.00), and a tax category (shopping_mall_tax_categories.id). The product can optionally be associated with a category through the shopping_mall_product_categories junction table, but this is handled separately after product creation.

Security: Only authenticated sellers can create products. This is enforced through the authorizationActors field, which accepts only ['seller'] actor types. The system validates that the authenticated seller has active status before processing the request.

The created product record is stored in the shopping_mall_products table with the following field mappings:
- title → shopping_mall_products.title
- description → shopping_mall_products.description
- price → shopping_mall_products.price
- shopping_mall_seller_id → mapping from JWT authenticated actor
- shopping_mall_tax_category_id → provided in request body
- status → automatically set to 'draft' initially
- created_at, updated_at → automatically set

The response returns the newly created product as a complete object with all fields, including the generated ID and timestamps. This allows the client to immediately use the returned product object for subsequent operations like associating images or categories.

Related operations: GET /products/{productId} retrieves the product after creation. PATCH /products allows searching products. PUT /products/{productId} updates an existing product (requires product status to be 'draft').

Error handling: Returns 400 Bad Request if validation fails (wrong title length, price out of range, invalid tax category). Returns 401 Unauthorized if the user is not authenticated as a seller. Returns 403 Forbidden if the seller account is not active.

requestBody.description: Creation data for a new product listing.

responseBody.description: The newly created product object with all fields including generated ID and timestamps.

The product must be in 'draft' or 'published' status to be updated. Seller identity is extracted from the authentication token and verified against the product owner. Updates to published products trigger a moderation review if significant changes are detected.

Security: Only the owning seller or platform administrators can update products. The operation validates that all field changes comply with content policies and business rules (minimum/maximum character lengths, price ranges, etc.). The updated_at timestamp is automatically set to the modification time.

Special handling: When a product's status changes from 'draft' to 'published', it triggers validation of all associated product variants and images to ensure completeness. Products with missing required information cannot be published. Products that have been archived cannot be updated.

Related operations: GET /products/{productId} to view current product details before update, and DELETE /products/{productId} to permanently remove products.

This is a hard delete operation performed only on products with 'draft' status. Products that are 'published' cannot be deleted directly — they must first be archived and then purged through a separate system process after a retention period.

operations.description:
Create a new product variant (SKU) for an existing product.

This operation allows sellers to define specific configurations of a product (e.g., color, size, style) as distinct inventory items with unique pricing and stock levels. Each variant is uniquely identified by its SKU (Stock Keeping Unit) and is linked to the parent product.

The operation validates that:
1. The specified parent product exists and is published (status: 'published')
2. The SKU is globally unique across all products and variants
3. The price is within acceptable business limits ($0.01 to $5000.00)
4. The inventory_count is non-negative
5. The attributes JSON string is properly formatted

This creates an independent inventory unit that can be tracked and sold separately from the parent product. The new variant inherits product metadata (title, description, tax category) but maintains separate pricing and stock. Once created, the variant immediately becomes available for sale and appears in product search results with its specific configuration.

Related operations:
- GET /products/{productId}/variants: Retrieve all variants of a product
- PUT /products/{productId}/variants/{variantId}: Update an existing variant

This operation allows sellers to modify the attributes of an existing product variant such as price, inventory count, or variant-specific title. Changes take effect immediately, affecting product display, search results, and purchase availability.

The operation validates that:
1. The target variant exists and belongs to the specified parent product
2. The parent product is still published (status: 'published')
3. The SKU cannot be changed (it is immutable after creation)
4. Updated price is within acceptable business limits ($0.01 to $5000.00)
5. Updated inventory_count is non-negative
6. The attributes JSON string, if updated, is properly formatted

Important: Only attributes specific to the variant can be modified. The parent product's core information (title, description, tax category) remains unchanged. Modified variants maintain their association with the parent product and remain subject to the parent's active status. Inventory changes trigger automated inventory transaction logs for audit purposes.

Permanently delete a specific product variant from the shoppingMall catalog. This operation removes the variant record entirely from the database and cancels all associated inventory allocations and reservations. This action is irreversible and affects the product's availability to customers.

The variant must not have any pending orders or active checkouts associated with it. If any linked cart items or order items reference this variant, the deletion will fail with an appropriate error code.

This operation does not affect the parent product, only the specific variant identified by variantId. The variant's inventory records will be purged from shopping_mall_inventory_units, and all related inventory transactions will be marked as cancelled. Any references to this variant in shopping_mall_product_variants will be permanently removed.

Successive attempts to access this variant from API endpoints (products/{productId}/variants/{variantId}|at, products/{productId}/variants|index) will return a 404 Not Found error.

The deletion is flagged with the system's auditing system via shopping_mall_data_change_logs, recording the actor who performed the deletion and timestamp.

It follows a hard delete pattern as variants are considered substitutable entities, and product variations should not persist indefinitely in the system.

The response includes a pagination structure to handle products with large image collections.

operations.description:
Retrieve all tags associated with a specific product in the shoppingMall catalog. This operation operates on the shopping_mall_product_tags_products junction table that establishes the many-to-many relationship between products and tags. The endpoint returns a comprehensive list of all tags applied to the specified product, including tag name, description, and display order.

This operation functions as a search/list endpoint with filtering capabilities, sorted by the display_order field to ensure consistent UI presentation. Each tag returned is an individual record from the shopping_mall_product_tags table, linked through the shopping_mall_product_tags_products junction table.

Security: This is a public read operation. Any user, authenticated or not, can retrieve product tags. The system does not restrict tag visibility based on user roles or permissions since tags are public categorization metadata.

Implementation note: This operation performs a JOIN between shopping_mall_products, shopping_mall_product_tags_products, and shopping_mall_product_tags tables to return tag data. It selects ONLY the tag properties (name, description, slug, display_order) from the shopping_mall_product_tags entity, excluding product-related data to maintain clean separation of concerns. The results are ordered by display_order to ensure consistent presentation in UI components that rely on tag ordering for navigation or filtering.

This is a detail retrieval operation (GET) that returns a single tag object when the product-tag relationship exists. If the specified tag is not associated with the product or does not exist, the system returns a 404 Not Found error.

Security: This is a public read operation. Any user, authenticated or not, can retrieve specific product-tag associations. Tags are public categorization metadata and are not subject to access controls based on actor roles.

Implementation note: This operation performs a JOIN between shopping_mall_products, shopping_mall_product_tags_products, and shopping_mall_product_tags tables to verify the existence of the relationship and retrieve the tag's complete properties. Unlike the index operation, this returns a single tag object with all its fields (name, slug, description, display_order) instead of an array. The system does not return product information in this response; it only returns tag information as the response body type is ISshoppingMallProductTag, which represents the tag entity itself.

This is a many-to-many relationship deletion that does not remove the tag or product records from the system. The tag and product remain intact and can be re-associated later if needed. This operation is used when a seller wants to remove a tag from a product's categorization without deleting the tag itself, which may be used by other products.

The shopping_mall_product_tags_products table has a composite primary key of (shopping_mall_product_id, shopping_mall_category_id), and this operation removes the specific record matching the provided product and tag identifiers. This is not a soft delete; the relationship record is permanently removed.

This operation assumes that the user has permission to modify the product's tags. The operation is restricted to the product's owner (seller) or administrators. The product's status (draft/published/archived) does not affect the ability to remove tags.

This operation returns a paginated list of product categories, enabling functionality for product category browsing, filtering, and management. The associated categories are retrieved through the shopping_mall_product_categories junction table, which links products with categories from the shopping_mall_categories table.

The operation supports pagination, sorting, and filtering by category attributes including category name, description, and hierarchy levels. This allows customers and sellers to browse product categories efficiently and find products within specific category groupings. The response includes detailed category information, not just IDs, enabling rich UI displays.

The shopping_mall_product_categories table has a composite primary key of (shopping_mall_product_id, shopping_mall_category_id), and this operation retrieves all records matching the provided product ID. The response includes category details from the shopping_mall_categories table, performing a JOIN operation to provide enriched category information.

This operation is designed to be read-only and is accessible to both authenticated users and anonymous users, as category information is generally public and non-sensitive. The operation does not affect any data in the system; it only retrieves existing associations.

Related operations: POST /products/{productId}/categories to add a category to a product, DELETE /products/{productId}/categories/{categoryId} to remove a specific category from a product, PATCH /categories to search for available categories, GET /categories/{categoryId} to get detailed information about a specific category.

This operation fetches the relationship between a specific product and its assigned category. It verifies that the product is indeed linked to the requested category in the shopping_mall_product_categories junction table. The product's status and category's active status are checked to ensure both entities are in valid states.

This operation is primarily used in product management interfaces and category exploration features where users need to confirm the hierarchical relationship between products and categories.

The data returned corresponds to the shopping_mall_product_categories table, with additional context from shopping_mall_products and shopping_mall_categories to validate that both entities are active and properly configured.

- PATCH /products/{productId}/categories: Lists all categories assigned to a product
- GET /categories/{categoryId}/products: Lists all products assigned to a category

The operation requires the product to be in 'draft' status, as published products cannot have their categories modified directly. If the product is 'published', this operation will fail with a 403 error. Seller ownership verification is performed to ensure the caller has permission to modify the product.

This functionality enables sellers to refine product categorization during the product creation process before publication. Once a product is published, category changes require creating a new product or using an alternatives such as duplication.

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of shopping carts from the system. This operation operates on the shopping_mall_carts table from the Prisma schema and provides advanced search capabilities for finding carts based on customer, status, and expiration criteria.

The operation supports comprehensive pagination with configurable page sizes and sorting options. Carts can be sorted by creation date, expiration date, status, or last update in ascending or descending order.

Security considerations include rate limiting for search operations and appropriate filtering of cart data based on the requesting user's authorization level. Only users with appropriate permissions can access detailed cart information, while basic cart summaries may be available to authenticated users.

This operation integrates with the shopping_mall_carts table as defined in the Prisma schema, incorporating all available cart fields and relationships. The response includes cart summary information optimized for list displays, with options to include additional details based on authorization level.

Related operations: Retrieve a specific cart (GET /carts/{cartId}), Create a new cart (POST /carts), Update a cart (PUT /carts/{cartId}), Delete a cart (DELETE /carts/{cartId}).

responseBody.description: Paginated list of cart summary information matching search criteria

Retrieve detailed information about a specific shopping cart by its unique identifier.

The cart data is linked to the shopping_mall_customer table via shopping_mall_customer_id, ensuring proper ownership validation. Only authenticated customers can access their own carts. Admin users may access any cart for support purposes.

The cart item data is not included in this response to maintain performance. To view cart items, use the dedicated /carts/{cartId}/items endpoint.

Related operations: List all carts (PATCH /carts), Create a new cart (POST /carts), Update a cart (PUT /carts/{cartId}), Delete a cart (DELETE /carts/{cartId}).

operations.description:
Create a new shopping cart for a customer.

This operation allows authenticated customers to create a new shopping cart that serves as a temporary workspace for selecting products for purchase. Each cart is uniquely associated with a specific customer and has a 24-hour expiration period for logged-in users (7 days for anonymous users). The cart begins in 'active' status and can contain multiple cart items that represent product selections.

The cart creation process automatically assigns a unique identifier, sets the creation and update timestamps, and initializes the expiration time based on the user's authentication status. No cart items are added during creation - they must be added separately through the cart items endpoint.

This operation is related to shopping_mall_carts table in the Prisma schema and is used as the starting point for the customer purchasing workflow. After creating a cart, customers typically add items using the POST /carts/{cartId}/items endpoint.

Security: Only authenticated users can create carts. The customer_id is automatically derived from the authentication token and cannot be specified in the request body. Anonymous users can create carts but have a longer expiration period for better user experience.

Related operations: GET /carts/{cartId} to retrieve cart details, PUT /carts/{cartId} to update cart status or properties, POST /carts/{cartId}/items to add products to the cart.

requestBody.description: Creation parameters for a new shopping cart.

responseBody.description: The newly created shopping cart with its assigned ID and metadata.

operations.description:
Update an existing shopping cart's properties.

This operation allows customers to modify the state of their shopping cart after creation. Valid updates include changing the cart's status (for example, from 'active' to 'checked_out' when a customer is ready to checkout), or updating cart-level properties for experience improvements.

According to the Prisma schema for shopping_mall_carts, the cart can have status values: active, expired, or checked_out. This endpoint specifically enables transitioning a cart from 'active' to 'checked_out' as part of the checkout process. Other properties like expires_at, created_at, and updated_at are automatically managed by the system and cannot be modified through this API.

Security: Only the cart owner (authenticated user) can update their cart. The system validates that the cart_id in the path matches the authenticated user's cart.

Important business rule: When a cart's status is changed to 'checked_out', the system automatically initiates the order creation workflow, converting all cart items into order items, reserving inventory, and creating payment transactions.

Related operations: POST /carts to create a new cart, POST /carts/{cartId}/items to add products to cart, DELETE /carts/{cartId} to cancel a cart, GET /carts/{cartId} to retrieve cart details.

operations.description:
Permanently removes a shopping cart and all its associated items from the system.

This operation performs a hard delete of the cart record, removing it entirely from the database. All cart items linked to this cart are also permanently deleted in a cascading operation.

This endpoint is intended for user-initiated cart deletion where the customer wishes to completely remove their shopping session. The cart cannot be recovered after deletion. The operation cannot be undone.

The cart deletion is immediate and does not follow soft delete patterns. Even carts that were previously marked with a deleted_at timestamp will be permanently removed when this endpoint is invoked.

This operation invokes native database cascading deletes through the foreign key relationship between shopping_mall_carts and shopping_mall_cart_items. The associated cart items are automatically removed by the database due to their CASCADE deletion constraint.

Authorization: Only the cart owner (authenticated customer) can delete their own cart. The system verifies ownership by comparing the authenticated user ID with the cart's shopping_mall_customer_id.

Error scenarios: Returns 404 if cartId does not exist or if the authenticated user does not own this cart. Returns 403 if the user is not authenticated.

operations.description:
Retrieves all cart items associated with a specific shopping cart, providing a comprehensive view of the customer's current selections.

This operation queries the shopping_mall_cart_items table to return all active items contained within the specified cart. It returns both the cart item details and links to the product variant information, allowing display of complete item information including product name, variant options, price, and quantity.

The operation supports filtering of items by status (active, out_of_stock, removed, checked_out) through request parameters, though these parameters are typically not required for basic cart retrieval. The default behavior returns all cart items regardless of status. This endpoint is optimized for performance and returns results in a single query with appropriate joins to product variant data.

Security: The cart item access is owned by the cart, which is owned by the customer. The system verifies that the authenticated user owns the cart before returning any items. Unauthorized access to another user's cart items is strictly prohibited.

Performance: This endpoint is designed to be efficient since cart items are retrieved in a single query with a simple JOIN between shopping_mall_cart_items and shopping_mall_product_variants.

Note: This operation differs from the DELETE /carts/{cartId} endpoint which removes the entire cart and all associated items. This endpoint only retrieves the items while preserving the cart structure and allowing modifications.

Related operations: POST /carts/{cartId}/items (add items), PUT /carts/{cartId}/items/{item_id} (update item quantity), DELETE /carts/{cartId}/items/{item_id} (remove specific item).

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific cart item from a customer's active shopping cart. This operation operates on the shopping_mall_cart_items table and returns detailed information about a single product variant selected by the customer. The cart item data includes the quantity, unit price (captured at time of addition), and current status to ensure price stability during checkout even if product prices change later. This endpoint is typically called when the customer examines individual items in their cart before proceeding to checkout. Security: Only the cart owner can access items in their own cart. The system validates that the cart_id in the path parameters corresponds to a cart owned by the authenticated customer. This operation integrates with the shopping_mall_cart_items table structure and references the shopping_mall_carts and shopping_mall_product_variants tables to ensure data consistency. When this operation is requested, no other endpoints need to be called directly, but the associated cart must be in 'active' status to return item details.

When a customer views their cart, the system may call this operation multiple times to render each cart item individually, or alternatively customers may call the index operation to retrieve all items in a single request.

Related operations:
- GET /carts/{cartId}/items (index) - to retrieve all cart items
- PATCH /carts/{cartId}/items/{itemId} - to update cart item quantity
- DELETE /carts/{cartId}/items/{itemId} - to remove item from cart

Add a new product variant to a customer's active shopping cart. This operation operates on the shopping_mall_cart_items table and creates a new cart item record that captures the product variant, quantity, and unit price at the exact moment of addition. This ensures price stability during checkout even if the product price changes later. The operation validates that the cart exists, is in an active status, and has sufficient inventory for the requested quantity.

Security: Only authenticated customers can add items to their own active cart. The system automatically associates the cart item with the authenticated customer's cart_id. When a product is added to cart, inventory is not reserved immediately, but the system validates the current availability. If inventory becomes unavailable before checkout, the cart item status transitions to 'out_of_stock'. This operation integrates with the shopping_mall_cart_items table and references the shopping_mall_carts and shopping_mall_product_variants tables to ensure data integrity. No other endpoints need to be called to successfully execute this operation, but the associated cart must be in 'active' status.

Related operations:
- GET /carts/{cartId}/items/{itemId} (at) - to view individual cart item details
- PATCH /carts/{cartId}/items/{itemId} - to update quantity of existing item
- DELETE /carts/{cartId}/items/{itemId} - to remove item from cart

operations.description:
Update a specific item within a customer's shopping cart.

This operation modifies the quantity or status of an individual cart item identified by its unique cart and item IDs. When a customer adjusts their cart (increasing/decreasing item quantity or removing an item from purchase intent), this endpoint handles the modification with atomic validation.

The operation validates that the cart exists and is still active (not expired or checked out), that the cart item belongs to the specified cart (enforced by foreign key constraint), and that the new quantity does not exceed the current inventory of the product variant. The price is not modified as it was captured at the time of cart addition to ensure purchase consistency.

Security: Only the cart owner (authenticated customer) can modify cart items. The cart's customer_id is verified against the authenticated user's identity.

State transitions:
- If quantity becomes 0, item.status transitions to 'removed'
- If inventory becomes insufficient after quantity adjustment, item.status transitions to 'out_of_stock'
- If quantity increases and inventory becomes available, item.status transitions back to 'active'

This operation directly modifies the shopping_mall_cart_items table and is atomic - either all changes succeed or none do.

Related Operations:
- GET /carts/{cartId}/items - View all items in a cart
- DELETE /carts/{cartId}/items/{itemId} - Remove the item from cart
- POST /carts/{cartId}/items - Add a new item to cart
- PATCH /carts/{cartId} - Check out the entire cart

operations.description:
Remove a specific item from a customer's shopping cart.

This operation permanently removes an individual cart item from the cart, reducing the cart's total item count and value. Unlike marking an item as 'removed' in status, this operation deletes the cart item record entirely from the database.

The operation validates that the cart exists and is still active (not expired or checked out), that the cart item belongs to the specified cart (enforced by foreign key constraint), and that no other system processes are currently modifying this item. This prevents race conditions during cart modifications.

Security: Only the cart owner (authenticated customer) can remove items from their cart. The cart's customer_id is verified against the authenticated user's identity.

After removal, the system does not track this specific cart item any longer. For audit purposes, the removal event may be logged separately in shopping_mall_audit_logs table.

This is a hard delete operation that permanently removes the record. The cart item record is not subject to soft deletion.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of all wishlists created by the authenticated customer, ordered by most recently updated. This operation provides a comprehensive view of all active wishlists associated with the current user, allowing them to manage multiple collections of products they are interested in for future purchase.

The operation supports pagination with configurable page size and supports sorting by creation date or update date. Customers can browse their entire collection of wishlists to identify which lists contain products they're considering for future purchase.

There are no creation, update, or deletion of wishlists through this operation - these are handled through separate endpoints. This endpoint is read-only and specifically designed for listing and discovery of existing wishlist collections.

The data returned represents wishlist summaries rather than full details, as the purpose is to provide an overview for selection. Detailed product lists within each wishlist are accessible via the specific wishlist endpoint.

This operation corresponds to the shopping_mall_wishlists Prisma model, retrieving records where deleted_at is null to show only active wishlists that the customer has not removed. The operation automatically filters results to only include wishlists belonging to the authenticated customer based on the JWT token information.

Retrieve detailed information of a specific wishlist identified by its unique identifier. This operation returns comprehensive data for the requested wishlist including its name, creation timestamp, update timestamp, and the complete list of wishlist items with product variant references.

The operation verifies that the authenticated user owns the requested wishlist before returning the data, ensuring privacy and access control. The response includes a full list of items in this wishlist, each containing the product variant ID, when the item was added to the wishlist, and any optional notes the customer has added.

This is a detail view operation providing all necessary information about a single wishlist that a customer has selected for in-depth review. While the wishlist listing endpoint returns summaries, this endpoint returns complete details including the contained items.

The data structure corresponds to the shopping_mall_wishlists Prisma model for wishlist metadata and the shopping_mall_wishlist_items Prisma model for the items within this wishlist. The operation performs a JOIN between these tables to return the complete dataset relevant to this wishlist.

The operation excludes any wishlist items that have been soft-deleted (where deleted_at is non-null), ensuring only active products of interest are displayed. The operation will return a 404 error if the wishlist_id does not correspond to any active wishlist owned by the authenticated customer.

Create a new wishlist for the authenticated customer.

This operation allows a customer to create a personalized wishlist for future product consideration. Each wishlist is associated with the authenticated user's account and can be named descriptively for organizational purposes (e.g., "Future Gifts", "Travel Essentials").

The system validates that the wishlist name is unique within the customer's account. Due to the composite unique constraint on (shopping_mall_customer_id, name) in the shopping_mall_wishlists table, each customer can have only one wishlist per name.

The created wishlist will have automatic timestamps for creation and update, and will be initially empty of items. It will be immediately accessible through the customer's profile and can be modified by adding product items.

Security: Only authenticated customers can create wishlists.

Update an existing wishlist's name or metadata.

This operation allows a customer to modify an existing wishlist, such as renaming it or updating its metadata. The wishlist must belong to the authenticated customer.

The system enforces the composite unique constraint on (shopping_mall_customer_id, name) from the shopping_mall_wishlists table. When updating the wishlist name, the system verifies the new name doesn't already exist for the same customer to prevent duplicate names. If the name is not changed, only the updated_at timestamp is modified.

This operation does not allow modification of wishlist items - those are managed through separate endpoint. The wishlist's creation timestamp remain immutable.

Security: Only the authenticated customer who owns the wishlist can perform this operation.
Related operations: GET /wishlists (list customer's wishlists), DELETE /wishlists/{wishlistId} (soft delete wishlist), POST /wishlists/{wishlistId}/items (add items to wishlist).

operations.description:
Permanently delete a user's wishlist and all its associated items. This operation performs a hard delete of the wishlist record from the database, removing it entirely and making it unrecoverable. The corresponding wishlist items are automatically removed through database cascade deletion. This action is irreversible and should be used with caution.

This operation directly targets the shopping_mall_wishlists model and must be performed by the owner of the wishlist. operations.description:
Retrieve the payment details for a specific order using its unique order number.

This operation fetches the complete payment information associated with an order, including payment status, amount, currency, transaction ID, and processing timestamp. The payment record is maintained in a 1:1 relationship with the order entity in the database, and this endpoint provides read-only access to this financial data.

Security: This operation requires authentication as the order owner or an administrator. The order number serves as a human-readable identifier that maps to the internal UUID-based order ID. The payment details are returned in the order's currency and include all financial metadata recorded at the time of payment processing.

Implementation: The system joins the shopping_mall_orders table with the shopping_mall_order_payments table using the order_number as a lookup key and returns a structured payment record with all relevant financial fields.

Related operations: PUT /orders/{orderNumber}/payment (update payment status for pre-authorized transactions), GET /orders/{orderNumber} (retrieve order summary including payment status).

parameters.name: orderNumber
parameters.description: Unique human-readable identifier for the order in format ORD-YYYYMMDD-NNNNN. Must exactly match the order_number field in the shopping_mall_orders table.

responseBody.description: Complete payment details for the specified order, including financial information and processing status.

operations.name: at

prerequisites.description: Order must be created before payment details can be retrieved

operations.description:
Update the payment status for a specific order using its unique order number.

This operation allows internal systems and authorized administrators to update the payment status of an order, typically for handling payment gateway failures, manual payment confirmations, or fraud review outcomes. The payment status can transition between: pending, processing, authorized, captured, failed, refunded, or chargeback.

Security: This operation can only be performed by system services or administrators. Regular users cannot update payment status; this is strictly a backend administrative function. The operation is idempotent and validates that the target order exists and is in a state that permits payment status changes.

Business Logic: Changes to payment status trigger downstream workflow events like order status updates, inventory reservation adjustments, and notification generation. This endpoint does not process real payments; it updates the system's record of payment status based on external payment gateway events.

Implementation: The system updates the shopping_mall_order_payments table with the new payment_status value and logs the change in the shopping_mall_order_status_history table. The payment amount and currency remain immutable once recorded.

Related operations: GET /orders/{orderNumber}/payment (retrieve payment details), GET /orders/{orderNumber} (retrieve order summary with current payment status).

parameters.name: orderNumber
parameters.description: Unique human-readable identifier for the order in format ORD-YYYYMMDD-NNNNN. Must exactly match the order_number field in the shopping_mall_orders table.

requestBody.description: New payment status and optional approval details for the order payment.

responseBody.description: Updated payment record with new status and timestamp.

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed shipping information for a specific order using its unique order number. This operation accesses the shopping_mall_order_shipping table to return comprehensive delivery details including recipient information, carrier data, and tracking information. The order_number field serves as the primary reference since it's globally unique and designed for human readability, avoiding UUID-based identifiers. The shipping data represents the state of delivery information at the time of order processing, allowing accurate historical retrieval even if customer addresses change later. This operation supports the business need to provide customers with real-time shipping status updates and allows customer support to access complete delivery details for inquiries.

When an order reaches the 'pending_payment' status, a corresponding shopping_mall_order_shipping record is created with the customer's provided shipping address. The tracking_number and tracking_url fields are populated when the seller marks the order as shipped, enabling customers to monitor delivery progress through carrier websites. The estimated_delivery_date is calculated based on the selected shipping method and destination, while real_delivery_date is recorded when confirmed by the carrier's system.

Security considerations: This read operation is available to the order's customer (the authenticated user who created the order) and to administrative personnel. The operation uses the order_number parameter rather than the internal ID to expose a user-friendly identifier, while maintaining security through careful authorization validation against the customer-seller relationship.

Related operations: Update shipping details (PUT /orders/{orderNumber}/shipping), List all orders for a customer (PATCH /orders).

parameters.name: orderNumber
parameters.description: Unique business identifier code of the target order (global scope). This operates as the primary key for order retrieval and follows the format ORD-YYYYMMDD-NNNNN as defined in the shopping_mall_orders schema.

responseBody.description: Complete shipping details including recipient information, carrier, tracking details, and estimated delivery data.

operations.name: at

prerequisites.description: Order must be created before shipping details can be retrieved

operations.description:
Update the shipping information for a specific order using its unique order number. This operation modifies the shopping_mall_order_shipping record associated with the target order, allowing updates to delivery details before the order is marked as shipped. The order_number field serves as the primary reference since it's globally unique and designed for human readability, avoiding UUID-based identifiers.

Required fields include recipient name, address components, and contact phone number. Updates can modify any portion of the shipping information except the associated order ID (which remains fixed). This operation is designed for use during the order preparation phase, particularly when customers need to correct delivery addresses after placing an order but before fulfillment begins. After shipping, this endpoint becomes read-only.

When the order status is 'draft' or 'pending_payment', customers can modify their shipping details. The system validates all address components against international formatting standards and requires at minimum: first_name, last_name, address_line1, city, state, postal_code, and country. The phone field is required for carrier delivery attempts.

The carrier field cannot be modified via this operation as it's determined by the shipping method selection. Tracking_number and tracking_url fields are system-managed and updated automatically by sellers or fulfillment systems when the order is progressed to 'shipped' status. Manual updates to tracking information are prohibited to maintain data integrity and prevent fraudulent activities.

Security considerations: Only the customer who created the order can update its shipping information. Admins can also modify shipping details for support purposes, but must provide proper justification in audit logs. This prevents unauthorized alterations to delivery addresses that could facilitate fraud or theft.

Related operations: View shipping details (GET /orders/{orderNumber}/shipping), List all orders for a customer (PATCH /orders).

parameters.name: orderNumber
parameters.description: Unique business identifier code of the target order (global scope). This operates as the primary key for order retrieval and follows the format ORD-YYYYMMDD-NNNNN as defined in the shopping_mall_orders schema.

requestBody.description: Shipping information fields to be updated for the order.

responseBody.description: Updated shipping details containing all fields after successful modification.

operations.description:
Retrieve return records associated with a specific order using its order number.

This operation performs a search across all return requests linked to the order identified by the provided orderNumber. It returns a paginated list of return records with comprehensive details about return status, requested products, refund amounts, and processing history.

The system uses the orderNumber to locate the internal UUID-based order record, then retrieves all return records associated with that order through the shopping_mall_order_returns table's foreign key relationship. The operation supports filtering by return status and sorting by return date.

This is a read-only operation that does not modify any return records. The response includes summary information for each return, with links to detailed return records if needed.

Authorization: Any authenticated user can search for returns on their own orders. Admin users can search for returns across all orders.

Related operations: POST /orders/{orderNumber}/returns (to create a new return request) and GET /returns/{returnId} (to retrieve a specific return record details).

parameters.name: orderNumber
parameters.description: Unique order identifier in format ORD-YYYYMMDD-NNNNN. Must be globally unique and exactly match the orderNumber field in the shopping_mall_orders table.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of return records associated with the specified order, including summary information for each return.

operations.name: index

operations.description:
Submit a return request for an order. This operation creates a new return record that initiates the return workflow for products associated with the specified order.

When a customer submits a return request, the system validates that the order exists and is in a state that permits returns (paid, delivered, or completed). The request captures the primary return reason and any additional details provided by the customer. The system then creates a return record linked to the order and places the return in 'requested' status awaiting admin review.

This operation fulfills the requirement for customers to initiate return processes and creates the necessary audit trail of return intent. The actual processing (approval, receipt of items, refund issuance) requires separate administrative actions and is not performed by this endpoint.

Security: Customers can only create return requests for orders they have placed. The system validates ownership by matching the authenticated user's ID against the order's customer ID.

Related Operations: PATCH /orders/{orderNumber}/returns (to retrieve return status), PUT /orders/{orderNumber}/returns (to update return request), GET /orders/{orderNumber}/returns (to view existing return requests)

responseBody.description: The newly created return request record

operations.description:
Retrieve the current return request status and details for a specific order. This operation fetches all return records associated with the given order number and provides comprehensive information about each return request, including its current status, reason, refund amount, and processing progress.

The operation returns return data for all return requests issued against the specified order, supporting scenarios where multiple products may be returned in separate requests. Returns are sorted chronologically with the most recent first. Only returns with statuses 'requested', 'approved', 'awaiting_return', 'received', or 'refunded' will be included in the response; denied or completed returns may be excluded based on business policy.

This endpoint supports an authenticated user viewing their own return requests. Admins can view return requests for any order. The response includes full return details but excludes sensitive administrative notes that may be in the raw system logs.

Security: Users can only access return information for orders they have placed. Administrators can view return information for all orders. The system performs strict ownership validation before returning any data.

Implementation note: This operation retrieves data from the shopping_mall_order_returns table, joining with all related information such as the original order details and customer information when appropriate. The operation returns a complete Return entity for each return record, including timestamps, refund amounts, and status history.

Related Operations: POST /orders/{orderNumber}/returns (to create a new return request), PUT /orders/{orderNumber}/returns (to update return request)
