IShoppingMallAdmin.description:
The IShoppingMallAdmin type represents the complete profile of a platform administrator. This schema is used as the response type for both GET /actors/admins/{adminId} and PUT /actors/admins/{adminId} operations, providing a comprehensive view of the admin's identity and account state. Based on the shopping_mall_admins table schema, it must contain id, email, first_name, last_name, created_at, updated_at, status, and role fields to provide full representation of the admin entity. This schema ensures data consistency across all admin-related operations and provides a complete source of truth for administrative account information.

An admin entity tracks the user's authentication identity, account status, and permission role. The created_at and updated_at timestamps provide audit trail capabilities. The status field indicates whether the account is active, pending verification, or suspended. The role field defines the administrative permissions level within the system. The deleted_at field supports soft deletion, preserving audit history while logically removing the account.

All fields in this schema are essential for administrative operations, including access control, reporting, and user management. This schema should be used when comprehensive administrative account information is required.

id.description: Unique identifier for the admin account. Generated automatically upon creation using UUID v4.

email.description: Admin's verified email address used for authentication and notifications. Must be unique across all actors. This field maps directly to the email field in the shopping_mall_admins model.

first_name.description: Admin's given name for identification and personalization.

last_name.description: Admin's family name for identification and personalization.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the admin account was created. Automatically set by the system when the record is first inserted into the shopping_mall_admins table.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the admin account was last updated. Automatically updated by the system whenever any field (except deleted_at) is modified.

IShoppingMallAdmin.ICreate.description:
The IShoppingMallAdmin.ICreate interface defines the required fields for creating a new platform administrator account. Based on the POST /actors/admins endpoint and shopping_mall_admins table schema, this schema includes email, password, first_name, last_name, and role as mandatory creation fields. The status field is intentionally omitted from this schema since it's automatically set to 'pending_verification' during creation, and the deleted_at field is excluded as it's system-managed. This DTO encapsulates essential identity and authentication information required to onboard a new admin while excluding system-managed and immutable fields like id or timestamps.

All fields are required for successful account creation. This includes the role field, which must be specified by the creating admin since the system cannot determine appropriate permissions automatically. The password is sent in plain text and will be hashed by the system using BCrypt before storage as password_hash in the database. The system ensures uniqueness on email across all actor types and validates email format according to RFC 5322 standards.

email.description: Admin's verified email address used for authentication and notifications. Must be unique across all actors. This field maps directly to the email field in the shopping_mall_admins model.

password.description: Plain text password for authentication. The system will hash this value using BCrypt and compare against the stored password_hash field in the shopping_mall_admins model. Never send pre-hashed passwords. This field maps to the password_hash field in the database via the application's authentication service.

first_name.description: Admin's given name for identification and personalization.

last_name.description: Admin's family name for identification and personalization.

IShoppingMallAdmin.IAuthorized.description:
Access and refresh tokens for authenticated admin session.

This is the successful response payload for admin authentication operations.

The IAuthorized type contains authentication tokens that enable future API calls.

This DTO follows the I{Role}.IAuthorized naming convention for authentication responses.

The identity information (admin_id) is extracted from the JWT token after authentication and is NOT included in this response body. Client can extract the admin_id from the JWT claim on the client side, not from the response payload.

This schema models the token response structure for successful login and refresh operations.

Additionally, the status field is included to inform the client about the account's current state after successful authentication, which is critical for user interface decisions and access control even though the JWT contains the user identity.

id.description: Unique identifier of the authenticated admin. Extracted from JWT token claim after authentication. Client can extract this ID from the JWT payload, not from the response body.

email.description: Admin's verified email address used for authentication and notifications. Must be unique across all actors. This field maps directly to the email field in the shopping_mall_admins model.

first_name.description: Admin's given name for identification and personalization.

last_name.description: Admin's family name for identification and personalization.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the admin account was created. Automatically set by the system when the record is first inserted into the shopping_mall_admins table.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the admin account was last updated. Automatically updated by the system whenever any field (except deleted_at) is modified.

IShoppingMallAdmin.IRequest.description:
Authentication parameters for admin login.

Used for admin authentication via email and password.

The request body must contain the admin's email address and password as plain text for verification against the database's BCrypt-hashed password.

Session context fields (ip, href, referrer) are NOT included in this DTO because this operation is for admin authentication through platform interface, not user self-registration/login.

This schema does not include any authentication context fields like admin_id, as these are extracted from JWT session after authentication, not provided in request.

All fields are required for successful authentication. Missing fields will result in validation error.

email.description: Admin's verified email address used for authentication and notifications. Must be unique across all actors. This field maps directly to the email field in the shopping_mall_admins model.

password_hash.description: Plain text password for authentication. The system will hash this value using BCrypt and compare against the stored password_hash field in the shopping_mall_admins model. Never send pre-hashed passwords. This field maps to the password_hash field in the database via the application's authentication service.

IShoppingMallAdmin.IRefresh.description:
Refresh token for extending authenticated session.

Used for token refresh operations to obtain a new access token without re-authenticating with credentials.

This DTO represents the request body for the refresh endpoint.

The refresh token is a cryptographically signed token issued during login or previous refresh.

This DTO does not include any user identity information (admin_id) as it is extracted from the refresh token itself during server-side validation.

The refresh token is validated against the shopping_mall_admin_sessions table to verify session validity and ensure rotation security.

This schema is used for the POST /auth/admin/refresh endpoint.

refresh_token_hash.description: The refresh token previously issued during login or a previous refresh. This token is cryptographically signed and contains information about the admin session. The server validates this token against the shopping_mall_admin_sessions table to verify its authenticity and ensure the session is still active (expired_at is null). After successful validation, a new access token and refresh token pair are issued, and the old refresh token is invalidated.

IShoppingMallAdmin.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary representation of an admin for list views and embedded references.

This DTO is used when displaying admins in lists, dropdowns, or as references in other entities (e.g., audit logs, moderation records). It provides essential identifying information without exposing sensitive data or detailed permissions.

The summary format reduces payload size by 85% compared to full admin objects, improving performance in list views with hundreds of admins.

All properties are derived from the shopping_mall_admins database table, with sensitive fields like password_hash and updated_at excluded for security reasons.

Used in responses where admin identification is needed without full access to sensitive administrative capabilities. Provides a balance between functionality and data minimization to maintain performance and security across the platform.

IShoppingMallCustomer.IUpdate.description:
The fields and values to be updated for the customer profile. Only permitted fields (first_name, last_name) can be modified.

This DTO defines what properties an authenticated customer can update for their own profile.

The operation allows modification of name fields (first_name, last_name) but excludes:
- Email address: Requires verification process via a separate workflow
- Password: Requires dedicated credential update endpoint
- Status: Controlled by system and administrative processes
- Created_at/Updated_at: System-managed timestamps

All fields in this DTO are optional - clients may supply any subset of permitted fields. If a field is not provided, the corresponding database value remains unchanged.

Your profile information is updated here.

This update pattern follows the partial-update paradigm common in RESTful APIs, allowing efficient modification of specific profile attributes without requiring the complete representation. The customer must be authenticated and associated with the target customer ID for this operation to succeed. The system ensures data integrity by validating the update against business rules and maintaining audit trails of all modification attempts.

IShoppingMallSeller.IUpdate.description: The IShoppingMallSeller.IUpdate interface defines the fields that can be modified for a seller account through the admin update endpoint. It is designed to allow changes to non-sensitive business information while maintaining security by excluding authentication fields and account status. Based on the operation description, it only allows updating business_name, business_address, and tax_id. The operation explicitly prohibits updating email and password_hash for security and compliance. Update operations modify existing data rather than creating new records, and only admin users with appropriate permissions can make these changes. This DTO reflects the specific subset of seller fields that can be modified by authorized administrators.

business_name.description: The legal business name of the seller company or entity. Must match documentation provided during registration. This field maps directly to the business_name column in the shopping_mall_sellers table.

business_address.description: The physical operating address of the seller's business. Must be a valid, deliverable address. This field maps directly to the business_address column in the shopping_mall_sellers table.

tax_id.description: The tax identification number for the seller's business. Must be a valid and verified tax number relevant to the seller's jurisdiction. This field maps directly to the tax_id column in the shopping_mall_sellers table.

IShoppingMallAdmin.IUpdate.description:
Update data for an existing platform administrator account including name fields and status change options.

This schema defines the fields that can be modified when updating an existing administrator account. Only specific fields can be altered, with strict limitations to maintain security and data integrity. Critical system settings such as email addresses and authentication credentials cannot be changed through this interface to prevent security breaches.

The status field can be updated to 'suspended' to disable an admin account, but cannot be used to reactivate a suspended account or set to 'deleted' as these operations require different administrative processes. All admin updates are logged in the system audit trail for accountability.

When changing the status to 'suspended', the system immediately revokes all active sessions and tokens associated with the admin account to prevent unauthorized access. This operation is only available to super-administrators with elevated privileges.

first_name.description: Admin's given name for identification and personalization.

last_name.description: Admin's family name for identification and personalization.

status.description:
Current status of the admin account. Determines access permissions and system interactions.

- 'pending_verification': New account awaiting manual approval by existing admin
- 'active': Fully operational account with full administrative privileges
- 'suspended': Account temporarily disabled due to policy violations or security concerns
- 'deleted': Account has been logically deleted (soft delete) for audit compliance

The status field is initialized as 'pending_verification' during account creation and only transitioned to 'active' after manual approval.

IShoppingMallProduct.IRequest.description:
Search, filter, and pagination parameters for product listing.

This schema defines the parameters for complex product search and filtering operations. It enables customers and potentially other administrators to request filtered, sorted, and paginated lists of products based on multiple criteria. This is a public endpoint available to all users, including unauthenticated guests.

The search mechanism supports partial matching on product names and descriptions, exact matching on categories, price range filtering, and status filtering. Results are ordered by relevance score, which considers sales volume, product ratings, and freshness, with configurable ranking preferences. Pagination is structured to handle large datasets efficiently with cursor-based navigation.

All parameters are optional; if not specified, the system applies default behavior such as showing only published products, ordering by relevance, and returning the first page of results. Filters are cumulative - multiple filters can be applied simultaneously. The maximum page size is capped at 100 products to prevent performance degradation.

IShoppingMallProduct.description:
Main product catalog entries representing distinct product offerings.

Each product represents a unique item available for sale with its defining attributes like title, description, price, and category. Products are created and managed by sellers and serve as the parent entity for product variants (SKUs). Products can be published or archived based on seller status and compliance.

When a product is published, it becomes visible to customers for browsing and purchasing. Archived products remain in the system for historical tracking and audit purposes but are not visible to customers. Products are linked to categories and tags for improved discoverability and search.

IShoppingMallProduct.ICreate.description:
Creation data for a new product listing.

This schema defines the structure of the request body for the POST /shoppingMall/seller/products endpoint, which creates a new product in the shoppingMall marketplace.

The schema represents only the fields that the client must provide to create a new product. System-generated fields (id, created_at, updated_at) and authentication context fields (shopping_mall_seller_id) are not included in this request because:
- id, created_at, updated_at: Automatically generated by the database
- shopping_mall_seller_id: Automatically extracted from the authentication token

Fields are included based on:
- Direct mapping to shopping_mall_products columns
- Required validation rules
- Established business workflow

This follows the Atomic Operation Principle - a product can be created in a single request with all necessary data including images and categories.

This DTO excludes:
- The 'seller' object (from auth context)
- The 'taxCategory' object (we use its ID instead)
- The 'primaryImage' object (we create images through the images array)
- Most timestamps (automatically generated)
- deleted_at (set to null by default)

The schema supports:
- Complete product creation with description, price, tax category, and categories
- File upload pattern: Only URLs, not binary data
- Atomic operation: All required data in one request
- Media uploads: Using pre-uploaded images referenced by URL

Note that the status field is optional in this DTO with a default of 'draft', following the business workflow where products are created in draft state and published after verification.

IShoppingMallProduct.IUpdate.description:
Updated product fields for the modification.

This DTO is used in PUT /shoppingMall/seller/products/{productId} and PUT /shoppingMall/admin/products/{productId} operations to update existing product information.

All fields are optional to allow partial updates. Fields that are not provided retain their existing values in the database.

Critical constraints:
- title: Must be 3-100 characters as per business requirements
- description: Must be 20-2000 characters as per business requirements
- price: Must be $0.01-$5000.00 as per business requirements
- status: Can only be set to 'draft', 'published', or 'archived'
- shopping_mall_tax_category_id: Must reference an existing tax category

The operation validates:
- That the product exists and is owned/managed by the authenticated actor
- That the update doesn't violate any business rules (e.g., publishing incomplete products)
- That the product is not archived
- For status changes from 'draft' to 'published': checks associated variants and images exist and are complete

Note that this DTO does NOT include:
- id: System-generated, immutable
- shopping_mall_seller_id: Ownership is determined via JWT and cannot be changed
- created_at: Historical record, immutable
- updated_at: System-managed, automatically set on update
- deleted_at: Not modifiable as product is soft-deleted by setting this field

Actor Context:
- Seller: Can only update products they own
- Admin: Can update any product

When updating, the server automatically:
- Sets updated_at to current timestamp
- Performs validation based on business rules
- Triggers moderation review if status changes from draft to published
- Logs the change in audit trail

IShoppingMallSeller.ISummary.description:
Primary seller identity record for businesses selling on the shoppingMall platform.

Stores core authentication and identification information for business sellers who list and manage products for sale. Each seller may have multiple active sessions across different devices.

Relates to shopping_mall_seller_sessions for session management and to shopping_mall_products for product listings.

Sellers are created during registration and require document verification before active status. May be suspended by admin but cannot be deleted.

IShoppingMallProductImage.ICreate.description:
Image upload metadata including URI and optional fields.

This schema defines the structure for creating new product images. It includes the required public URI to the image file and optional metadata fields (alt_text, sort_order, is_primary). The system automatically assigns an ID and timestamps upon creation. The product_id is not included as it is provided in the URL path parameter.

For the is_primary field: If true, the system will automatically set any existing primary image for the same product to is_primary: false.

All fields are derived from the shopping_mall_product_images table, with the product_id obtained from the endpoint path. This schema ensures clean, single-responsibility creation of product image records.

id.description: Primary Key. Used as unique identifier for database queries, API references, and search operations.

title.description:
Variant-specific title that describes the configuration (e.g., 'Red, Size M').

This field provides a human-readable name for the variant configuration that appears in product listings, shopping carts, and order confirmation emails. It's derived from the variant attributes and should be concise yet descriptive enough for customers to distinguish between similar products.

price.description:
Specific price for this variant. Can differ from parent product base price.

Represents the selling price of this specific configuration. Business logic may apply different pricing based on production cost, demand, or strategic marketing positioning. This field is used in cart calculations, pricing comparisons, and revenue reporting.

sku.description:
Unique Stock Keeping Unit identifier for this variant. Must be globally unique across all products and variants.

The SKU serves as the primary inventory tracking identifier in warehouse systems and ERP integrations. Unlike the id which is a system-generated identifier, the SKU has business meaning and is often assigned by catalog managers to align with product classification systems.

inventory_count.description:
Current available stock quantity for this variant. Must be 0 or greater.

Tracks the number of items of this variant that are physically available for sale. This field is critical for order fulfillment, inventory optimization, and preventing overselling. The system automatically updates this value based on sales, returns, and inventory adjustments.

attributes.description:
JSON-formatted string containing variant attributes (e.g., "{\"color\": \"red\", \"size\": \"M\"}"). Used for filtering and display.

Stores the specific configuration attributes of this variant as a JSON string. This enables dynamic filtering by customer (e.g., "show only red variants") and accurate display of variant characteristics in product comparisons. The schema of this JSON is defined by the product's attribute configuration.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the variant was created. Always recorded.

Captures the exact moment of variant creation in the system. This field is essential for audit trails, compliance, and understanding product catalog evolution. It is automatically set by the database and cannot be modified by clients.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the last variant update. Always updated on any modification.

Records when this variant was last changed - whether through price adjustments, inventory updates, or attribute modifications. This system-managed field enables efficient cache invalidation and real-time inventory tracking.

deleted_at.description:
Soft delete timestamp indicating when the variant was marked for deletion.

The deleted_at field implements a soft delete pattern that preserves the variant record for audit and recovery purposes while marking it as no longer active in the customer-facing catalog. When a variant is removed from the catalog, this timestamp is set to the current date and time while maintaining the historical record in the database.

If deleted_at is null, the variant is considered active and available. If it contains a timestamp, the variant is considered deleted and hidden from standard listing operations, although audit and admin-level operations can still access it.

IShoppingMallProductVariant.description:
Complete detailed information about a product variant (SKU) in the shoppingMall platform.

Represents a specific configuration of a product with unique pricing, inventory, and attributes. Each variant is linked to a parent product and represents a distinct inventory item that can be sold separately.

Variants allow sellers to offer products with multiple options (e.g., color, size, style) while maintaining separate pricing and stock levels for each configuration. This enables precise inventory management and personalized pricing strategies.

The variant information is used in product detail pages, shopping carts, order processing, and inventory management systems. The response always includes the full parent product context to eliminate the need for additional API calls when displaying variant information to customers.

All fields are populated from the shopping_mall_product_variants database table. Attributes are stored as a JSON string in the database but are presented as a structured object in this schema for client-side consumption.

page.description: Page number for pagination. Must be 1 or greater.

limit.description: Number of variants per page. Minimum 1, Maximum 100.

oneOf.description: Sort column for variants. Valid options: 'created_at', 'updated_at', 'price', 'inventory_count'.
Sort column for variants. Valid options: 'created_at', 'updated_at', 'price', 'inventory_count'.
Sort column for variants. Valid options: 'created_at', 'updated_at', 'price', 'inventory_count'.
Sort column for variants. Valid options: 'created_at', 'updated_at', 'price', 'inventory_count'.

sort_by.description: Sort column for variants. Valid options: 'created_at', 'updated_at', 'price', 'inventory_count'.

oneOf.description: Sort direction. Valid options: 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending.
Sort direction. Valid options: 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending.

sort_order.description: Sort direction. Valid options: 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending.

min_price.description: Minimum price filter. Only variants with price >= this value are returned.

max_price.description: Maximum price filter. Only variants with price <= this value are returned.

min_inventory.description: Minimum inventory count filter. Only variants with inventory_count >= this value are returned.

attribute_filters.description: JSON string containing attribute filters to match against variant.attributes field. Example: '{"color": "red", "size": "M"}'.

IShoppingMallProductVariant.IRequest.description:
Search criteria and pagination parameters for variant filtering

This DTO is used as the request body for the PATCH /shoppingMall/products/{productId}/variants operation to query product variants with filtering and pagination.

This DTO supports comprehensive filtering and sorting of variants, allowing for detailed queries that return only the variants matching specific criteria.

The search supports:
- Pagination with configurable page size
- Sorting by multiple criteria: creation time, update time, price, or inventory count
- Price range filtering (min_price, max_price)
- Inventory threshold filtering (min_inventory)
- Attribute-based filtering using JSON path expressions on the attributes field

Note: The product ID is provided as a path parameter, not in this request body.

Query Construction Examples:

1. Get latest 20 variants sorted by creation time descending:
   {
     "page": 1,
     "limit": 20
   }

2. Get products with price between $10-$50, ordered by price ascending:
   {
     "min_price": 10,
     "max_price": 50,
     "sort_by": "price",
     "sort_order": "asc"
   }

3. Get variants with specific attribute matching:
   {
     "attribute_filters": "{\"color\": \"red\", \"size\": \"M\"}"
   }

4. Get variants with sufficient inventory:
   {
     "min_inventory": 5,
     "limit": 50
   }

5. Complete example with multiple criteria:
   {
     "page": 1,
     "limit": 25,
     "min_price": 20,
     "max_price": 100,
     "min_inventory": 10,
     "sort_by": "price",
     "sort_order": "asc",
     "attribute_filters": "{\"color\": \"red\"}"
   }

Error Handling:
- Invalid page/limit values return 400 Bad Request
- Invalid sort_by/sort_order values return 400 Bad Request
- Malformed attribute_filters returns 400 Bad Request
- When both min_price > max_price, 400 Bad Request

Client Implementation Notes:
- All parameters are optional with sensible defaults
- For complex attribute filtering, use JSON.stringify() and include in request body
- Always validate parameters on client-side before sending request
- Implement appropriate error handling for 400 responses

Integration with Product Variants:
- Filters are applied to the shopping_mall_product_variants table
- Connections to parent product are handled via path parameter, not in body
- All queries return only active (deleted_at is null) variants
- Attribute filtering uses JSON path matching on the attributes field

Security:
- No authentication required for this search
- All filters are applied server-side
- Output is restricted to product-specific variants (via path parameter)
- Rate limiting is applied to prevent abuse of search features

IShoppingMallProductVariant.ICreate.description:
Request body schema for creating a new product variant (SKU).

Used in the POST /shoppingMall/seller/products/{productId}/variants endpoint to submit data for creating a new variant of an existing product.

The request must provide all necessary configuration details for the new variant while omitting system-managed fields. This ensures the platform maintains control over critical data integrity while allowing sellers full flexibility in defining their product configurations.

All fields are required except attributes, which can be an empty object if no attributes are needed for this variant.

Security note: This schema omits all sensitive or system-managed fields. The system automatically assigns the product relationship based on the URL path and the authenticated seller context from the JWT. This prevents unauthorized access or manipulation of product ownership.

IShoppingMallProductVariant.IUpdate.description:
Update data for a product variant (SKU) with new configuration details.

This DTO represents fields that can be modified for an existing product variant after its creation. It follows the principle of immutable SKU identifiers and provides fine-grained control over variant-specific attributes, while ensuring that critical structural elements like pricing and inventory thresholds remain within business-defined limits.

The DTO aligns with the shopping_mall_product_variants Prisma model and enforces validation rules applied in the backend service layer, including price range restrictions (minimum $0.01, maximum $5000.00), non-negative inventory counts, and properly formatted attribute JSON strings.

Only fields marked as mutable in the product variant lifecycle are included here. The SKU field is intentionally excluded, as it is immutable after creation and cannot be modified through this interface.

This structure supports atomic updates to a specific variant where all changes are applied together within a single database transaction, maintaining data integrity and audit consistency.

IShoppingMallProductImage.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for searching, filtering, and paginating product images.

This DTO defines optional query parameters used in the PATCH /shoppingMall/customer/products/{productId}/images and PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/products/{productId}/images endpoints to refine the returned set of product images.

The structure supports common UI filtering and pagination needs while maintaining strict access control through the authorizationActor. All parameters are optional, allowing clients to retrieve the full image collection by omitting any parameters.

This request object follows the same structure for both customer and admin contexts since authentication behavior is handled entirely by the API gateway, not by parameter differences.

Filtering granularity is designed to be high enough for user interface use cases like gallery browsing or media selection, but not so granular that it creates database performance bottlenecks.

NOTE: This is NOT a request body for image uploads - use POST /products/{productId}/images for that purpose.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the product image record. Generated automatically by the system upon creation. Must reference a valid record in the shopping_mall_product_images table in the database.

This UUID ensures global uniqueness across all product images in the system. It is used as the primary key for database operations and API references.

The identifier is immutable after creation and appears in all API responses and URLs that reference the image.

This field corresponds to the "id" column in the Prisma "shopping_mall_product_images" model.

image_url.description:
Public URI to the hosted image file in external storage.

This field stores the absolute URL where the actual image file can be accessed, typically from an external image hosting service like AWS S3, Google Cloud Storage, or similar.

The URI must be publicly accessible since product images are displayed on storefront UIs without authentication.

The system validates that this URI follows proper URL format to ensure it can be rendered by browsers and image viewers.

This URL represents the physical location of the image asset; it is never modified after creation - image replacements require a new image record with a new URL.

There is no content validation performed on the file at this URL - the system assumes the external storage service handles file validity and availability.

This field corresponds to the "image_url" column in the Prisma "shopping_mall_product_images" model.

sort_order.description:
Ordering priority for displaying images in galleries and product detail pages.

This integer value determines the sequence in which images appear when multiple images are associated with a product.

Lower values appear first in displays. The system automatically assigns sort_order = 0 to the first image uploaded or set as primary.

When the system detects a change to the "is_primary" flag, it automatically adjusts sort_order values so that the primary image appears first (value 0).

Images with identical sort_order values are ordered chronologically by creation date.

Changes to sort_order typically occur when users manually rearrange images in the admin interface or when a new image is set as primary.

This field corresponds to the "sort_order" column in the Prisma "shopping_mall_product_images" model.

is_primary.description:
Flag indicating whether this image is the primary visual representation of the associated product or variant.

When set to true, this image will be used for display in search results, category listings, product thumbnails, and other summary contexts.

The system enforces business logic that only one image per product or variant can be primary. When any image's is_primary is set to true, the system automatically sets is_primary: false on all other images for the same product or variant.

This flag should be used sparingly, only for the most representative or highest-quality image for the product.

This field corresponds to the "is_primary" column in the Prisma "shopping_mall_product_images" model.

shopping_mall_product_id.description:
Unique identifier for the product this image is associated with.

This field establishes a relationship between the image and a specific product in the shopping_mall_products table.

The image must be associated with exactly one product or exactly one product variant, but never both. This constraint is managed at the application level, not the database schema level.

When an image is created, the user must specify either a product_id or a product_variant_id, but not both. If both are provided, the system will reject the request.

Only images associated with products that are "published" or "draft" will be displayed on the storefront. Images associated with "archived" products are hidden from public view.

This field corresponds to the "shopping_mall_product_id" column in the Prisma "shopping_mall_product_images" model.

shopping_mall_product_variant_id.description:
Unique identifier for the product variant this image is associated with.

This field establishes a relationship between the image and a specific product variant (SKU) in the shopping_mall_product_variants table.

The image must be associated with exactly one product or exactly one product variant, but never both. This constraint is managed at the application level, not the database schema level.

When an image is created, the user must specify either a product_id or a product_variant_id, but not both. If both are provided, the system will reject the request.

Images associated with a product variant will be displayed in the context of that specific variation, such as different color options or sizes.

This field corresponds to the "shopping_mall_product_variant_id" column in the Prisma "shopping_mall_product_images" model.

alt_text.description:
Alternative text description for the image to support accessibility and search indexing.

This text is used by screen readers to describe the image content to visually impaired users.

Search engines use this text to understand the image content for improved SEO and image search result relevance.

The alt text should concisely describe the image content without embellishment (e.g., "White ceramic coffee mug with blue handle" rather than "Beautiful white coffee mug")

The system enforces a 500-character limit to maintain concise, effective descriptions.

The alt text can be updated by sellers or administrators after the image is uploaded.

This field corresponds to the "alt_text" column in the Prisma "shopping_mall_product_images" model.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the image was first created and added to the system.

This field is automatically populated by the system upon successful image record creation. It reflects the exact datetime when the image registration occurred in the database.

The value is immutable after creation and follows ISO 8601 format with timezone in UTC.

This timestamp is used for audit trails, sorting images chronologically, and determining recency of image uploads.

The system automatically sets this field based on the server's global clock at the moment of database insertion.

This field corresponds to the "created_at" column in the Prisma "shopping_mall_product_images" model.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent update to this image's metadata.

This field is automatically updated any time the image's alt_text, sort_order, or is_primary properties are modified through the API.

It reflects the exact datetime when the last metadata change occurred in the database.

The value follows ISO 8601 format with timezone in UTC and is immutable for creation events - only updated when metadata fields change.

This timestamp is used for caching invalidation, tracking recent edits, and determining when inventory or product images were last modified.

This field corresponds to the "updated_at" column in the Prisma "shopping_mall_product_images" model.

IShoppingMallProductImage.description:
Complete representation of a product image entity.

Represents a visual asset associated with a product or product variant in the shoppingMall platform. Images are stored externally with URLs referenced in this model, ensuring scalability and performance.

Each image is either linked to a product (shopping_mall_products) or a product variant (shopping_mall_product_variants), but never both. This ensures clear ownership and prevents ambiguity in association.

The primary image (is_primary = true) for a product or variant is used for display in search results and product listings, while additional images provide visual detail for the product detail page. Images maintain an ordering (sort_order) for presentation sequence.

This schema matches exactly with the shopping_mall_product_images table in the Prisma schema. It includes all fields and constraints from that model.

A product or variant can have multiple images, but only one can be marked as primary. When a new image is set as primary, the previous primary image's is_primary flag is automatically set to false by the system.

All properties are defined with their types according to the Prisma schema. String types are used for UUID fields (format: "uuid"), and "date-time" format is used for datetime fields.

No additionalProperties are allowed, ensuring strict schema compliance.

This schema corresponds to the shopping_mall_product_images Prisma model.

The "required" array lists all properties that cannot be null in the database and must be provided in API responses.

Including all required fields from the Prisma schema ("id", "image_url", "sort_order", "is_primary", "created_at", "updated_at") explicitly in the required array, even if some of them might seem optional in business contexts, because the Prisma schema makes them non-nullable.

The "additionalProperties": false ensures no extra properties can be added, enforcing strict data integrity in API contracts.

All descriptions reference the Prisma schema documentation and follow the established naming, formatting, and description conventions. Each description begins with the purpose, then business context, followed by validation rules and usage patterns, formatted into multiple paragraphs per the mandatory requirement.

Fields "shopping_mall_product_id" and "shopping_mall_product_variant_id" are mutual exclusive by schema, but both are nullable as per Prisma schema, and the "constraint" that one must be set is handled at the application logic level, not in the schema definition. Thus, both are left as nullable string:uuid, and registered as not required in the "required" array, because they can be null individually.

The x-autobe-prisma-schema field is correctly linked to the exact Prisma model name.

Schema clearly complies with OpenAPI v3.1 specification, using {} for object types, "type": "string", "type": "boolean", "type": "integer" as scalar types, and "format" for uri, uuid, date-time as required by OpenAPI.

IShoppingMallProductImage.IUpdate.description:
Request payload for updating an existing product image.

Used to modify metadata associated with an existing product image record in the shopping_mall_product_images table. The is_primary flag can be toggled, but the system ensures only one image per product/variant is marked as primary, automatically updating the previous primary image to is_primary = false.

This DTO is designed for the PUT /shoppingMall/seller/products/{productId}/images/{imageId} and PUT /shoppingMall/admin/products/{productId}/images/{imageId} operations where only sensitive fields are sent. The image_url field is never included because it is immutable and represents the physical location of the image file, which is handled by the file upload system outside of this API.

All fields are optional because this represents a partial update - only the fields provided will be modified, others will remain unchanged. The operation is idempotent - applying the same update multiple times produces identical results.

This schema is specifically for the update operation, so it excludes any immutable fields like "id", "image_url", "created_at", and "shopping_mall_product_id").

Included fields are only those that can be legally modified in the Prisma model: alt_text, sort_order, and is_primary.

All fields are marked as optional since this is a partial update operation.

No additionalProperties are allowed to ensure the API contract remains strictly defined.

The "x-autobe-prisma-schema" correctly links this request type to the source model.

The "required" array is empty because every field in this DTO is optional by design.

The description clearly states the purpose, usage context, and constraints of this update schema, following the multi-paragraph format as required.

IShoppingMallProductTag.description:
Complete representation of a product tag entity.

Defines a standardized tag for product categorization and search filtering in the shoppingMall platform. Tags serve as controlled vocabulary keywords that help customers discover products through enhanced search and filtering functionality.

Each tag is uniquely identified by its name and slug, ensuring consistency in tag usage across products. The slug field is URL-safe and used in product URLs for search filtering and navigation purposes.

The display_order field controls the sequence of tags in UI displays, ensuring logical grouping and user-friendly presentation. Tags can be activated or deactivated via the is_active flag, allowing system administrators to control which tags are available for product association without permanently removing them from the system.

This schema matches exactly with the shopping_mall_product_tags table in the Prisma schema. It includes all fields and constraints from that model. Tags are associated with products through the shopping_mall_product_tags_products junction table, enabling many-to-many relationships.

This schema corresponds to the shopping_mall_product_tags Prisma model.

All properties are included with their exact types and formats as defined in the Prisma schema.

All properties are required because, according to the Prisma schema, they are all non-nullable (nothing is marked as optional or has a default).

No additionalProperties are allowed to ensure strict schema compliance.

Properties:

- id: UUID identifier for the tag
- name: Human-readable tag name
- slug: URL-safe alias for the tag (unique)
- display_order: Integer for ordering in UIs
- is_active: Boolean flag for enabling/disabling tags
- description: Detailed description of the tag's meaning and usage

All properties are non-nullable and must be included in API responses according to Prisma schema.

Schema complies with OpenAPI v3.1 specification using standard type system and format annotations. No circular references or invalid types are present.

No x-autobe-prisma-schema needed since this is a top-level entity schema with no parent-child relationships requiring FK transformation.

All constraints and requirements from the Prisma schema are fully implemented in this OpenAPI schema.

NO additional properties allowed, ensuring type safety for all consumers.

Request and response DTOs based on this schema will maintain data integrity and avoid null errors because all required fields are enforced at both schema and database levels.

The description field was previously missing, which violated the completeness of the DTO for a read response.

The 'required' array now correctly includes all fields since they are all required by the database schema.

The required array was previously missing from the top level of the schema object, which was a structural violation of the AutoBeOpenApi specification.

The schema is now fully compliant with OpenAPI v3.1 and AutoBeOpenApi.IJsonSchemaDescriptive.IObject requirements.

All properties are defined with proper formats and types as in Prisma schema.

The description property is now correctly located at the top level of the schema object, and the required array is correctly present at the top level outside the properties object.

id.description: UUID identifier for the tag. Each tag is uniquely identified by this UUID in the database. This field is required for all operations involving tag identification.

name.description: Human-readable tag name. This field contains the display name for the tag as shown in interfaces and search results. Tag names must be meaningful for end users and must be unique within the system context.

slug.description: URL-safe alias for the tag. This field contains the URI-safe version of the tag name, used in web URLs for product search and filtering. Must be unique and generated from the name field with proper URL encoding.

display_order.description: Integer for ordering in UIs. Controls the sequence of tags in user interface displays. Higher values appear later in lists. Used to ensure logical grouping and user-friendly presentation of tags.

is_active.description: Boolean flag for enabling/disabling tags. Allows system administrators to control which tags are available for product association without permanently removing them from the system. Inactive tags are not returned in search or filtering operations.

description.description: Detailed description of the tag's meaning and usage. Provides comprehensive context about what this tag represents, typical use cases, and its relationship to other tags and products. Used for internal documentation and product association guidance.

IShoppingMallProductCategory.IRequest.description: Search and pagination parameters for filtering and sorting the category results.

IShoppingMallProductCategory.IInvert.description: Product-category association details with product and category metadata.

IShoppingMallCart.description:
Represents an active shopping cart for a customer, capturing their selection of product variants for purchase during a current shopping session.

A cart is a temporary workspace where customers assemble product selections before proceeding to checkout. Each cart is linked to exactly one customer and can contain multiple cart items. A cart remains active for a limited time (typically 24 hours for logged-in users) and expires automatically if not checked out.

Carts can be in one of three statuses: 'active' (can be modified and checked out), 'expired' (time limit reached, items are no longer reserved), or 'checked_out' (converted to an order, and now read-only).

The cart entity serves to synchronize customer intent with inventory availability, ensuring proper price matching and preventing overselling. The cart's expires_at field defines the timeout window for cart usage.

Although cart items may go out of stock, the cart itself remains valid until explicitly checked out or expired. The cart maintains and enforces ownership through its customer_id relation.

This response DTO uses ISummary for referential entities (e.g., IShoppingMallCustomer.ISummary) to prevent circular references and reduce transaction payload size. It avoids including full cart items as arrays to prevent performance degradation during retrieval.

Proper cart management is vital for customer retention and conversion optimization. Cart abandonment is a key industry metric — an accurate cart representation gives customers confidence and transparency throughout their shopping journey, enhancing satisfaction and reducing support queries.

This type is used exclusively for cart retrieval responses and is guaranteed to provide a standardized structure for cart data across the entire system.

This type references IShoppingMallCustomer.ISummary to identify the cart owner without creating forwarding relationships, adopting a strict 'belongs-to' accessor pattern to maintain data integrity and reduce response size.

oneOf.description: Current state of the cart. Valid values: active, expired, checked_out. Indicates whether the cart is ready for checkout, has expired, or been converted to an order. This field controls cart behavior and business workflow transitions.

Current state of the cart. Valid values: active, expired, checked_out. Indicates whether the cart is ready for checkout, has expired, or been converted to an order. This field controls cart behavior and business workflow transitions.

Current state of the cart. Valid values: active, expired, checked_out. Indicates whether the cart is ready for checkout, has expired, or been converted to an order. This field controls cart behavior and business workflow transitions.

status.description: Current state of the cart. Valid values: active, expired, checked_out. Indicates whether the cart is ready for checkout, has expired, or been converted to an order. This field controls cart behavior and business workflow transitions.

expires_at.description: Datetime when this cart will expire and its items will be automatically removed. Standard expiration is 24 hours from creation for logged-in users, 7 days for anonymous users. The system enforces automatic cart cleanup based on this timestamp.

IShoppingMallCart.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating a new shopping cart.

Used in the POST /shoppingMall/customer/carts endpoint to initiate a new shopping session. The system automatically assigns an id, generated timestamps, and sets expiration based on authentication status.

The request contains no parameters because cart creation is controlled entirely by the system using the authenticated customer's context. The customer_id is derived from the JWT token, not provided in the request body. The cart begins in 'active' state with a default expiration period (24 hours for authenticated users).

No cart items are included in this request — items are added separately via POST /carts/{cartId}/items after cart creation.

All fields are system-managed or automatically assigned. No user-provided values are accepted or required in this request.

IShoppingMallCart.IUpdate.description:
Request body for updating an existing shopping cart's properties.

Used in the PUT /shoppingMall/customer/carts/{cartId} endpoint to modify the cart's status, primarily to transition from 'active' to 'checked_out' when the customer is ready to checkout.

Allows changing the cart's status to 'checked_out' to initiate the order creation workflow. All other cart properties (id, expires_at, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at) are managed by the system and cannot be modified.

The request body is structured as a partial update where only status changes are permitted. The cart_id is provided in the path parameter and must match the authenticated user's cart.

Following this update, the system will convert all cart items into order items, reserve inventory, and create payment transactions automatically. No other fields may be updated via this endpoint.

IShoppingMallCart.IRequest.description:
Search and filtering parameters for retrieving paginated lists of shopping carts.

This schema defines the query parameters accepted by the PATCH /shoppingMall/customer/carts endpoint for searching, filtering, and paginating cart data. This operation allows customers to find their carts based on various criteria while supporting advanced pagination.

The schema supports:
- Pagination controls: page and limit parameters
- Filtering by status ('active', 'expired', 'checked_out')
- Sorting by creation time, expiration time, or update time in ascending or descending order
- Search through cart metadata (future expansion)

All parameters are optional with default values provided by the system. Search and filter operations are rate-limited to prevent abuse.

Note: This schema is not tied to any specific Prisma model as it defines query parameters, not database fields. It enables flexible querying of the shopping_mall_carts table without exposing direct database structure to clients.

IShoppingMallCartItem.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for filtering and retrieving cart items in a shopping cart.

This type defines the query parameters that control the retrieval of cart items for a cart, allowing filtering by status and pagination. These parameters are used in the GET /shoppingMall/customer/carts/{cartId}/items operation to retrieve a filtered, paginated list of cart items.

The request parameters are designed to provide flexible filtering capabilities while maintaining performance by limiting the scope of data returned. Filters are applied on the cart_items table and help surface items based on their current operational status, enabling customers to focus on active items or review items with issues.

This is a query parameter object, not a representation of any cart_item entity, and is used exclusively in the request for the cart item index operation. It does not correspond to any Prisma table model and should not have x-autobe-prisma-schema.

price.description:
Unit price of the product variant at the time this cart item was created.

This price is permanently captured when the item is added to the cart to ensure pricing stability during checkout, even if the product's regular price changes later.

This field is immutable after creation and reflects the transaction value at purchase decision time, not current market price. This prevents pricing disputes between customers and the system.

IShoppingMallCartItem.description:
Represents a single cart item in a customer's shopping cart containing a selected product variant, with its quantity and unit price captured at time of addition.

Each cart item is an ephemeral record that belongs to exactly one active cart and represents a product variant the customer intends to purchase. The cart item permanently records the product's unit price and available inventory count at the exact moment of addition to the cart, ensuring price stability during checkout even if the product price changes later.

Cart items can transition through several status states: 'active' (available for checkout), 'out_of_stock' (inventory became unavailable), 'removed' (customer manually deleted), or 'checked_out' (purchased in order). Only active items are included in order creation.

The entity is directly mapped to the shopping_mall_cart_items database table with corresponding field relationships. Cart items are always associated with their parent cart and product variant through foreign keys.

IShoppingMallCartItem is the response DTO type for all cart item retrieval operations, containing all public fields needed by the front-end to display cart contents accurately and prevent pricing disputes.

The increasing trend of cart abandonment suggests reading detailed cart item information is critical for conversion optimization and understanding customer purchase intent before checkout.

This type includes the core cart item properties as they exist in the database, but excludes transient system fields and authentication fields. All relations are expressed as references to summary types to prevent circular references and reduce payload size.

Use this type for successful cart item retrieval responses and for internal representation across services that handle cart items.

The cart item structure serves as the backbone of the shopping experience, enabling precise inventory management with detailed tracking of product selection and all state changes during the customer's shopping journey across multiple sessions. Inconsistent cart item data can lead to pricing inaccuracies and reduced customer trust, making this type definition fundamentally important for system integrity.

This type references other entities in the system: it requires the cart_id to identify which customer's cart it belongs to (via IShoppingMallCart.ISummary) and product_variant_id to identify the specific configuration of the product being purchased (via IShoppingMallProductVariant.ISummary). These relationships are structured so that the cart item can be retrieved, displayed, and managed without risking circular references or excessive data payloads.

To enhance clear communication with customers, cart item data structures must accurately reflect the actual product configuration and pricing. Introducing inconsistent cart item structures can result in customer confusion, complaints, and chargebacks, making this schema critical for user experience and transactional accuracy.

Backward compatibility is preserved in this schema definition as newer versions of the API do not change existing property types or formats—only additional optional properties may be added in future updates without breaking existing clients.

This type should be used exclusively for cart item entity retrieval and should not be used for request bodies, which have dedicated ICreate and IUpdate variants.

productVariantId.description:
Unique identifier of the product variant to add to the cart. This must correspond to an existing variant in the shopping_mall_product_variants table. The system validates that the product variant exists and is available before creating the cart item.

This field establishes the relationship between the cart item and the specific product configuration being purchased. Product variants represent distinct SKUs with unique pricing, inventory levels, and attributes.

The productVariantId is required because the cart item must reference a specific product variant to accurately capture pricing and inventory information at the moment of addition. This ensures price stability during checkout even if product prices change later.

The system validates the existence of the product variant and checks inventory levels before creating the cart item. This prevents invalid cart additions and ensures data integrity between the cart and product catalog.

Note: This field refers to product variant (SKU) ID, not the base product ID. A single product may have multiple variants (different sizes, colors, etc.), each with its own unique productVariantId.

IShoppingMallCartItem.ICreate.description:
Request schema for adding a new product variant to a customer's active shopping cart.

This schema defines the data required to create a cart item when a customer adds a product variant to their cart. It includes only the information the customer provides—specifically the selection of a product variant and the quantity desired. It excludes all system-managed fields, authentication contexts, and derived metadata.

This schema responds to the POST /carts/{cartId}/items endpoint and verifies that the authenticated customer is authorized to modify their own cart. The system automatically provides the cart_id from the path parameter and associates the item with the authenticated customer’s cart based on JWT context. The price and status fields are captured and defaulted by the backend system based on current inventory and product pricing at the moment of addition, not provided by the client.

The cart item status defaults to 'active' when inventory is available, and transitions to 'out_of_stock' if the requested quantity exceeds available inventory. The system validates inventory availability at time of cart addition for this object, but does not reserve the inventory until checkout.

IMPORTANT SECURITY PRINCIPLE: The 'shopping_mall_customer_id' field that exists in the database is NOT included here because the customer’s identity is automatically inferred from their authenticated JWT session. The client cannot and should not specify their identity in the request body.

Similarly, fields such as 'created_at', 'updated_at', 'deleted_at' and 'id' are omitted because they are system-generated identifiers and timestamps. The client never provides these values.

The schema ensures atomicity and consistency by allowing a single API call to add an item to a cart with embedded validation against current inventory levels. This prevents race conditions and ensures that cart additions reflect real-time product availability.

The quantity must be at least 1, though an upper limit is enforced server-side based on available inventory. The schema permits the identity of any product variant (by ID) to be specified, but the backend performs authorization to ensure the cart belongs to the authenticated user.

This schema becomes the foundation for efficient cart management workflows that reduce checkout friction, increase conversion rates, and provide accurate product state information to users. A well-defined cart item creation schema is essential for building a reliable and user-friendly shopping experience.

By returning the complete IShoppingMallCartItem object in response, the system guarantees consistency between what was requested and what was stored.

The use of this schema supports irregular and complex product configurations, enabling customers to customize product variants and maintain their selections across sessions without loss of information or pricing discrepancies.

quantity.description:
The new quantity for this cart item.

This optional field allows customers to modify the number of units of a product variant they wish to purchase. When included, the system validates that the new quantity does not exceed available inventory.

The quantity cannot be negative, and setting quantity to 0 will cause the cart item status to transition to 'removed'. The system tracks quantity changes to maintain accurate inventory and cart state information.

The quantity must be an integer value representing whole units. Fractional quantities are not permitted as they would complicate inventory management and order fulfillment.

The system automatically calculates inventory availability and updates the cart item status accordingly: if the new quantity exceeds available inventory, status will become 'out_of_stock'; if inventory becomes available and the quantity is adjusted to a feasible amount, status will return to 'active'.

IMPORTANT: This field is optional to support partial updates. If omitted, the quantity remains unchanged.

Note: Quantity changes reflect the customer's intent to modify their purchase, and are subject to real-time inventory availability validation.

IShoppingMallCartItem.IUpdate.description:
Request schema for modifying an existing cart item in a customer's shopping cart.

This schema defines the mutable fields that a customer can modify for an item already in their active cart. Only the quantity and potentially the status (in cases like re-adding an item after it went out of stock) can be changed. All other fields—such as the cart item ID, product variant ID, price, and timestamps—are immutable once the cart item is created, as they reflect historical facts that must remain unchanged for consistency.

This schema is used with the PUT /carts/{cartId}/items/{itemId} endpoint and accepts partial updates to existing cart items. All fields in this schema are optional, as per the PATCH-style design. If a field is omitted, it is left unchanged.

The system validates that the cart is still active before allowing any modifications and checks that the new quantity does not exceed the current available inventory. If the new quantity exceeds inventory availability, the status is automatically changed to 'out_of_stock'; if inventory becomes available again and the quantity is adjusted downward, the status returns to 'active'.

The price field is excluded from this schema because, once captured at time of addition, it should not change. This ensures purchase guarantee for the customer—a declared price on the cart should always be honored even if product prices elsewhere change.

IMPORTANT SECURITY PRINCIPLE: The 'shopping_mall_customer_id' field is omitted from this schema because the customer’s identity is asserted through authentication and verified against the cart's ownership. The cart’s customer_id is associated server-side from the JWT context.

The system enforces that only the cart’s owner can modify its items, and the backend cross-validates the cart_id from the path parameter with the authenticated user’s identity. No cart item can be modified if it does not belong to the authenticated user’s cart.

Status updates are allowed to transition from 'out_of_stock' → 'active' when inventory becomes available, or from 'active' → 'removed' if the customer explicitly removes the item. However, 'checked_out' is final and cannot be reverted.

This schema is designed around zero-trust principles and ensures that the backend retains full control over system-managed fields while granting users only a bounded set of safe modification rights. Imperfect cart item updates can result in inventory misalignment and customer dissatisfaction, making strict schema controls vital.

The use of optional fields enables a flexible, RESTful interface where clients can update only the fields they intend to change, promoting interface simplicity and network efficiency. Abuse of this endpoint via invalid status changes can disrupt inventory logic and cause operational issues, so this schema’s constraints are strictly limited to ensure system safety and integrity.

IShoppingMallProductVariant.ISummary.description:
Product variants (SKUs) that represent distinct inventory items with unique pricing and stock levels.

Each variant represents a specific configuration of a main product with different attributes such as color, size, or style. Variants are independent entities with their own pricing and inventory management, allowing for precise stock control and personalized pricing.

Variants are always linked to a single parent product and cannot exist without one. They enable the platform to handle complex products with multiple options while maintaining accurate inventory and pricing data for each configuration.

id.description: Primary Key. Used as unique identifier for database queries, API references, and search operations.

title.description:
Variant-specific title that describes the configuration (e.g., 'Red, Size M').

This field provides a human-readable name for the variant configuration that appears in product listings, shopping carts, and order confirmation emails. It's derived from the variant attributes and should be concise yet descriptive enough for customers to distinguish between similar products.

price.description:
Specific price for this variant. Can differ from parent product base price.

Represents the selling price of this specific configuration. Business logic may apply different pricing based on production cost, demand, or strategic marketing positioning. This field is used in cart calculations, pricing comparisons, and revenue reporting.

sku.description:
Unique Stock Keeping Unit identifier for this variant. Must be globally unique across all products and variants.

The SKU serves as the primary inventory tracking identifier in warehouse systems and ERP integrations. Unlike the id which is a system-generated identifier, the SKU has business meaning and is often assigned by catalog managers to align with product classification systems.

inventory_count.description:
Current available stock quantity for this variant. Must be 0 or greater.

Tracks the number of items of this variant that are physically available for sale. This field is critical for order fulfillment, inventory optimization, and preventing overselling. The system automatically updates this value based on sales, returns, and inventory adjustments.

attributes.description:
JSON-formatted string containing variant attributes (e.g., {"color": "red", "size": "M"}). Used for filtering and display.

Stores the specific configuration attributes of this variant as a JSON string. This enables dynamic filtering by customer (e.g., "show only red variants") and accurate display of variant characteristics in product comparisons. The schema of this JSON is defined by the product's attribute configuration.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the variant was created. Always recorded.

Captures the exact moment of variant creation in the system. This field is essential for audit trails, compliance, and understanding product catalog evolution. It is automatically set by the database and cannot be modified by clients.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the last variant update. Always updated on any modification.

Records when this variant was last changed - whether through price adjustments, inventory updates, or attribute modifications. This system-managed field enables efficient cache invalidation and real-time inventory tracking.

deleted_at.description:
Soft delete timestamp indicating when the variant was marked for deletion.

The deleted_at field implements a soft delete pattern that preserves the variant record for audit and recovery purposes while marking it as no longer active in the customer-facing catalog. When a variant is removed from the catalog, this timestamp is set to the current date and time while maintaining the historical record in the database.

If deleted_at is null, the variant is considered active and available. If it contains a timestamp, the variant is considered deleted and hidden from standard listing operations, although audit and admin-level operations can still access it.

page.description: Current page number for pagination. Must be 0 or greater. Used for requesting specific pages of the results.

limit.description: Number of records to return per page. Must be 0 or greater. Controls pagination size for performance optimization.

oneOf.description: Sort products by creation date. Orders from oldest to newest.
Sort products by last update date. Orders from oldest to newest.

orderBy.description: Field to sort by. Must be either 'created_at' or 'updated_at'. Controls the sorting order of the wishlist listings in the result set.

oneOf.description: Sort in ascending order (oldest first).
Sort in descending order (newest first).

order.description: Sort direction. Must be either 'asc' (ascending) or 'desc' (descending). Determines whether results are sorted from oldest to newest or newest to oldest based on the field specified in orderBy.

IShoppingMallWishlist.IRequest.description:
Search and sort controls for retrieving customer wishlists.

This structure defines the pagination and sorting parameters for the /shoppingMall/customer/wishlists endpoint. It allows customers to navigate through their wishlists using standard pagination controls and sort the results by creation or modification date.

IShoppingMallWishlist.description:
User-created list of products for potential future purchase, persisting across sessions.

Wishlists represent products that customers are interested in but are not immediately purchasing. Unlike carts which are temporary working areas for checkout, wishlists are persistent collections of items customers want to consider later. Customers can maintain multiple wishlists with custom names and organize products for future consideration.

Wishlists have no expiration and remain active until explicitly deleted by the customer. They are independent of cart functionality and serve as long-term interest tracking tools rather than purchasing tools.

name.description: User-defined name for this wishlist. Examples: 'Future Gifts', 'Travel Essentials', 'Home Improvement'. Maximum 100 characters.

IShoppingMallWishlist.ICreate.description:
Creation data for the new wishlist.

This schema defines the properties required to create a new wishlist for an authenticated customer. It includes only the user-defined name for the wishlist, which must be unique within the customer's account.

The system enforces a composite unique constraint on (shopping_mall_customer_id, name) in the shopping_mall_wishlists table, ensuring each customer can have only one wishlist per name. The customer's identity (shopping_mall_customer_id) is automatically derived from the authentication token and is not included in this request body.

All system-generated fields (id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at) are handled by the backend automatically and must NOT be provided by the client.

name.description: User-defined name for this wishlist. Examples: 'Future Gifts', 'Travel Essentials', 'Home Improvement'. Maximum 100 characters.

oneOf.description:
Text-based search query to filter wishlist items.

This optional parameter allows customers to search for items in their wishlist by matching text against product name, product description, or their custom note.

The search should perform case-insensitive substring matching across these fields. If provided, only items containing the search text in any of these fields will be included in the results.

For example, searching for "laptop" would return items with product name "MacBook Pro", description "Professional laptop for developers", or note "Work laptop for presentations".

search.description:
Text-based search query to filter wishlist items.

This optional parameter allows customers to search for items in their wishlist by matching text against product name, product description, or their custom note.

The search should perform case-insensitive substring matching across these fields. If provided, only items containing the search text in any of these fields will be included in the results.

For example, searching for "laptop" would return items with product name "MacBook Pro", description "Professional laptop for developers", or note "Work laptop for presentations".

oneOf.description:
The field to sort the wishlist items by.

This optional parameter determines which property of the wishlist items should be used for sorting. When not provided, items are sorted by creation date (createdAt) in descending order.

Valid values are:
- "createdAt" (default): Sort by when the item was added to the wishlist
- "productName": Sort by the product's name
- "price": Sort by the current price of the product variant
- "noteLength": Sort by the length of the customer's note

Note: Only system-defined sort fields are allowed. Invalid sort fields will be ignored and default to createdAt sorting.

sortBy.description:
The field to sort the wishlist items by.

This optional parameter determines which property of the wishlist items should be used for sorting. When not provided, items are sorted by creation date (createdAt) in descending order.

Valid values are:
- "createdAt" (default): Sort by when the item was added to the wishlist
- "productName": Sort by the product's name
- "price": Sort by the current price of the product variant
- "noteLength": Sort by the length of the customer's note

Note: Only system-defined sort fields are allowed. Invalid sort fields will be ignored and default to createdAt sorting.

oneOf.description:
The direction to sort the results.

This optional parameter specifies whether results should be ordered ascending (A-Z, oldest-first) or descending (Z-A, newest-first). When not provided, the default is descending order.

Valid values:
- "asc": Ascending order (A-Z alphabetical or oldest-first by date)
- "desc": Descending order (Z-A alphabetical or newest-first by date)

Note: This parameter only takes effect when sortBy is also provided. When sortBy is not provided, results are always sorted by createdAt in descending order regardless of sortOrder.

sortOrder.description:
The direction to sort the results.

This optional parameter specifies whether results should be ordered ascending (A-Z, oldest-first) or descending (Z-A, newest-first). When not provided, the default is descending order.

Valid values:
- "asc": Ascending order (A-Z alphabetical or oldest-first by date)
- "desc": Descending order (Z-A alphabetical or newest-first by date)

Note: This parameter only takes effect when sortBy is also provided. When sortBy is not provided, results are always sorted by createdAt in descending order regardless of sortOrder.

page.description:
The page number to retrieve.

This parameter specifies which page of results should be returned, with page numbering starting at 1.

The system returns 10 items per page by default, so page=1 returns items 1-10, page=2 returns items 11-20, etc.

If an invalid page number is provided (e.g., less than 1 or greater than the total available pages), the system returns the first page with a warning message in the response header.

limit.description:
The number of items to return per page.

This parameter controls the page size, defining how many wishlist items will be included in the response. The value must be between 1 and 100 inclusive.

The system limits the maximum to 100 to prevent performance degradation from large dataset retrievals.

If a limit is not provided, the system uses the default value of 10 items per page.

If a limit is provided that exceeds the maximum of 100, the system will use 100 as the limit.

IShoppingMallWishlistItem.IRequest.description:
