Search criteria, filters, and pagination parameters for retrieving wishlist items.

This schema defines the query parameters for listing items within a specific wishlist. It supports search functionality to filter items by product name, description, or custom note using text matching, as well as sorting and pagination controls for efficient data retrieval.

The request uses the IPageIShoppingMallWishlistItem.ISummary response type, so this schema focuses on parameters for filtering and organizing the list of wishlist items. The authenticated customer's identity is verified through authentication context and is not included in this request body.

Note that the wishlist_id parameter is provided in the path and is not included here as it's already contained in the URL.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the wishlist item.

This is the primary key of the shopping_mall_wishlist_items table and uniquely identifies each wishlist item record in the database.

The ID is auto-generated by the system upon creation and cannot be modified or assigned manually.

customerId.description:
Identifier of the customer who owns this wishlist item.

This foreign key links to the shopping_mall_customers table and establishes which customer has saved this wishlist item.

This field is immutable after creation and cannot be changed once the wishlist item is created. The system automatically populates this value based on the authenticated customer's identity from the JWT token.

wishlistId.description:
Identifier of the wishlist that contains this item.

This foreign key links to the shopping_mall_wishlists table and identifies which wishlist the product variant has been saved to.

This field is immutable after creation as it defines the permanent relationship between the wishlist and the product vote. The system validates that the wishlist exists and belongs to the authenticated customer during creation.

productVariantId.description:
Identifier of the product variant that has been added to the wishlist.

This foreign key links to the shopping_mall_product_variants table and points to the specific product SKU that the customer has saved for future consideration.

The system enforces a uniqueness constraint on the combination of wishlistId and productVariantId to prevent duplicate entries in the same wishlist. This ensures each product variant can only be saved once per wishlist.

oneOf.description:
Optional personal note that the customer can add to the wishlist item.

This field allows customers to add context or description for why they've saved a product to their wishlist. It might include gift occasions, size preferences, or other personal notes.

This field is optional and can be null. If provided, it's updated via PUT /wishlist/items/{itemId} and persisted in the database as a text field. The note can be modified at any time before the item is removed from the wishlist.

note.description:
Optional personal note that the customer can add to the wishlist item.

This field allows customers to add context or description for why they've saved a product to their wishlist. It might include gift occasions, size preferences, or other personal notes.

This field is optional and can be null. If provided, it's updated via PUT /wishlist/items/{itemId} and persisted in the database as a text field. The note can be modified at any time before the item is removed from the wishlist.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp when the wishlist item was created.

This field is auto-populated by the system at the time of object creation and represents when the customer first added the product variant to their wishlist.

All timestamps use ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ) and are stored in UTC. This field is immutable and cannot be modified after creation.

updatedAt.description:
Timestamp of the last update to this wishlist item.

This field is automatically updated whenever the customer modifies the item's note field via PUT /wishlist/items/{itemId}.

All timestamps use ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ) and are stored in UTC. This field reflects the last time any property of the wishlist item was changed.

IShoppingMallWishlistItem.description:
Individual items within a wishlist, representing products of potential future interest.

Wishlist items capture products that customers have expressed interest in for possible future purchase. Unlike cart items, wishlist items do not capture pricing at time of addition since prices may change over time and these are not immediate purchases.

These items persist indefinitely until removed by the customer and serve as long-term interest tracking rather than transactional records. Wishlist items are organized within their parent wishlist and can be reordered or annotated by the customer.

IShoppingMallWishlistItem.ICreate.description:
Create request body for adding a product variant to a wishlist. This type defines the required properties for creating a new wishlist item.

This DTO is used specifically for the POST /shoppingMall/customer/wishlists/{wishlistId}/items endpoint. When a customer adds a product variant to their wishlist, they provide the product_variant_id to establish the relationship between their wishlist and the product.

This DTO is designed to be minimal, containing only the critical information needed to create the relationship: the ID of the product variant and an optional customer note. It intentionally does not include any system-managed fields like IDs or timestamps, as these are auto-generated by the system.

The protected fields constraint requires that the authenticated customer's identity (customer_id) cannot be specified in the request body. The system extracts this information from the authenticated session (JWT token) and automatically associates the new wishlist item with the right customer. This is a critical security rule to prevent unauthorized access and impersonation.

The system enforces a uniqueness constraint on the combination of shopping_mall_wishlist_id and shopping_mall_product_variant_id. Multiple attempts to add the same product variant to the same wishlist will result in a failure response, preventing duplicates. This is handled at the database layer.

The note field is optional because not all customers want to add additional context when saving a product. This allows for both simple bookmarking and richer personalization depending on the customer's preference.

Important: This DTO does not represent a purchase intention. Its sole purpose is to track interest for future consideration. Therefore, it contains no payment, shipping, or quantity information that would be associated with a purchase.

The field naming follows the Prisma schema definition with the same casing (snake_case converted to camelCase in the API). The property shopping_mall_product_variant_id becomes productVariantId in the DTO to follow JavaScript/TypeScript naming conventions while maintaining the relationship reference clearly.

A prefix 'shopping_mall_' is preserved from the Prisma model name to maintain clear lineage and prevent ambiguity in a system that may have multiple domains.

This DTO is designed to be consumed by a frontend client that displays a 'Save to Wishlist' button on product pages. The button collects the variant ID and sends it to this endpoint.

Examples of good values:
- productVariantId: "dd33fdd2-bd8a-4a19-9917-5f39a0142a25" (valid UUID)
- note: "For birthday gift next month" (transparent human-readable content)

Examples of bad values:
- productVariantId: "not-a-uuid" (invalid format)
- productVariantId: "12345" (invalid type)

The request should be made with the target wishlist ID included in the path parameter, not in this body. The path parameter is authoritative and cannot be substituted with a request body value.

This creates an immutable record that can only be modified in terms of its note (via IUpdate) or removed (via DELETE). The chosen variant and wishlist relationship cannot be changed after creation.

No proprietary fields or non-standard types are used - only string types for UUID and optional text. Passwords, tokens, and sensitive data are prohibited in this request body as they would violate authentication boundary rules.

IShoppingMallWishlistItem.IUpdate.description: Updated information for a wishlist item, primarily focused on the customer's personal note.

IShoppingMallOrder.IRequest.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for order filtering.

id.description: Primary Key.

order_number.description: Unique order identifier in format ORD-YYYYMMDD-NNNNN. Must be globally unique.

subtotal.description: Total price of all items before taxes and shipping. Excludes discounts.

tax_amount.description: Total tax amount applied based on product categories and jurisdiction.

shipping_fee.description: Total shipping cost based on selected shipping method and destination.

discount_amount.description: Total discount applied from coupons or promotions.

total_amount.description: Final amount due after applying taxes, shipping, and discounts. subtotal + tax_amount + shipping_fee - discount_amount.

currency.description: Currency code for this order (e.g., USD, KRW, EUR). Must match ISO 4217 standards.

status.description: Current order status. Valid values: draft, pending_payment, paid, confirmed, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded, completed.

business_status.description: Additional business workflow status. Valid values: normal, fraud_review, refund_requested, return_requested, disputed, completed.

notes.description: Additional notes from customer during checkout. Limited to 500 characters.

created_at.description: Timestamp when this order was created. Always set during order draft creation.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when this order was last modified. Updated on status changes, shipping address updates, etc.

deleted_at.description: Timestamp when this order was soft-deleted. NULL if active. Used for order recovery and audit trails.

customer.description: Customer who placed this order. {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}.

seller.description: Primary seller responsible for fulfilling this order. {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}.

paymentMethod.description: Payment method used for this order. {@link shopping_mall_payment_methods.id}.

shippingMethod.description: Shipping method selected for this order. {@link shopping_mall_shipping_methods.id}.

IShoppingMallOrder.description:
Main order entity representing a customer's purchase transaction.

Captures the core details of each order placed through the shoppingMall platform. Each order is linked to a specific customer and contains product information, pricing, and overall order state. Orders can be modified during the checkout process but become immutable once payment is completed.

Orders form the central hub of the commerce workflow, connecting customers, products, payments, shipping, and returns. The order status progresses through defined lifecycle stages from creation to completion or cancellation.

All order entities (items, payments, shipping, returns) reference this parent order entity. Soft deletion supports order recovery before final cancellation.

The order entity follows the format from the shopping_mall_orders Prisma model, with all properties properly mapped. The description is sourced directly from the Prisma model comment.

All fields required for operation: Add or delete order, customer and seller assignment, and all order status tracking are included.

All fields not required for the operation are present to ensure complete business context and audit trail 

This schema receives the order update endpoint and returns the updated order state.

The schema has the following fields: 
- id: unique identifier for the order. normal identifier
- order_number: unique order identifier in format ORD-YYYYMMDD-NNNNN
- subtotal: total price of all items before taxes and shipping
- tax_amount: total tax amount applied based on product categories and jurisdiction
- shipping_fee: total shipping cost based on selected shipping method and destination
- discount_amount: total discount applied from coupons or promotions
- total_amount: final amount due after applying taxes, shipping, and discounts
- currency: currency code for this order (e.g., USD, KRW, EUR) 
- status: current order status. Valid values: draft, pending_payment, paid, confirmed, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded, completed
- business_status: additional business workflow status. Valid values: normal, fraud_review, refund_requested, return_requested, disputed, completed
- notes: additional notes from customer during checkout. Limited to 500 characters
- created_at: timestamp when this order was created
- updated_at: timestamp when this order was last modified
- deleted_at: timestamp when this order was soft-deleted. NULL if active. Used for order recovery and audit trails.
- shopping_mall_customer_id: customer who placed this order. reference to shopping_mall_customers.id
- shopping_mall_seller_id: primary seller responsible for fulfilling this order. reference to shopping_mall_sellers.id
- shopping_mall_payment_method_id: payment method used for this order. reference to shopping_mall_payment_methods.id
- shopping_mall_shipping_method_id: shipping method selected for this order. reference to shopping_mall_shipping_methods.id

All fields are required except: notes, shopping_mall_payment_method_id, shopping_mall_shipping_method_id, and deleted_at 

The type of each field matches the definition in Prisma schema, with string or number types as appropriate.

The description for each field references the corresponding Prisma schema comment.

Each field follows the format and constraints provided in Prisma schema.

All relationships are properly defined using $ref when pointing to other schemas.

This schema is an object type with all properties defined as required based on the Prisma schema and business requirements.

This schema's chirality supports both request and responses for the update operation.

items.description:
Individual product items within an order.

Represents the specific products, quantities, and pricing details of each item in an order. Each order item references a specific product variant and captures its price at the exact moment of purchase,
ensuring accurate historical records even if prices change later.

Order items are always created as part of order creation and are managed exclusively through their parent order. They have no independent existence outside of an order context.

The line item price reflects the exact price paid by the customer at purchase time, which may differ from the current product price due to promotions or price changes.

paymentMethod_id.description: Payment method used for this order. {@link shopping_mall_payment_methods.id}.

shippingMethod_id.description: Shipping method selected for this order. {@link shopping_mall_shipping_methods.id}.

notes.description: Additional notes from customer during checkout. Limited to 500 characters.

currency.description: Currency code for this order (e.g., USD, KRW, EUR). Must match ISO 4217 standards.

IShoppingMallOrder.ICreate.description:
Order creation data with cart items and shipping preferences.

Security: Only authenticated customers can create orders. The shopping_mall_customer_id is automatically populated from the JWT authentication token. The system validates that the customer has items in their cart and that the cart items reference valid, published products. Rate limiting applies to prevent automated bulk order creation.

This operation triggers automatic inventory reservations for items in the cart. Once payment is completed, the order status transitions from 'draft' to 'pending_payment', and inventory is officially assigned to the order.

IShoppingMallOrder.IUpdate.description:
Partial update fields for the order. Only fields that can be modified before payment processing can be included.

Describes the fields that are permitted to be updated for an order before payment processing is completed. This interface represents a PATCH-style update where only specified properties are modified.

The system recalculate tax_amount, shipping_fee, and total_amount automatically when this update is processed.

This interface supports the update operation on orders in 'draft', 'pending_payment', or 'confirmed' status. Once payment is processed, the order becomes immutable and cannot be updated through this interface.

Note that attempt to update any other fields (such as the items, customer, or seller information) will be rejected by the system.

This is an object type only with the following fields:
- notes: additional notes from customer during checkout. Limited to 500 characters
- shopping_mall_shipping_method_id: shipping method selected for this order. reference to shopping_mall_shipping_methods.id
- shopping_mall_payment_method_id: payment method used for this order. reference to shopping_mall_payment_methods.id

All fields are optional in this interface as this is a PATCH-style update.

The description of each field references the Prisma schema comment, and the format matches the Prisma schema definition.

The description for notes follows the Prisma schema comment: 'Additional notes from customer during checkout. Limited to 500 characters.'

The description for shopping_mall_shipping_method_id matches the Prisma schema comment: 'Shipping method selected for this order. {@link shopping_mall_shipping_methods.id}.'

The description for shopping_mall_payment_method_id matches the Prisma schema comment: 'Payment method used for this order. {@link shopping_mall_payment_methods.id}.'

All field types are strings with the appropriate format (uuid for ids, string for notes)

All fields use the same format as in the Prisma schema.

All fields are nullable (can be null or undefined).

id.description:
Unique identifier for the order item. This serves as the primary key in the database and follows UUID v4 standard for global uniqueness and security.

The ID is automatically generated by the system upon item creation and cannot be modified or assigned by users. It is used in API endpoints to uniquely identify individual order items across the entire system.

The UUID format ensures no collisions even in distributed systems and supports high scalability for thousands of concurrent order operations.

shopping_mall_order_id.description:
Parent order containing this item. References the unique identifier of the parent order in the shopping_mall_orders table.

This foreign key relationship ensures referential integrity between order items and their parent orders. Each order item belongs to exactly one order, and the system enforces that the referenced order must exist in the database.

The shopping_mall_order_id enables the system to quickly retrieve all items belonging to a specific order and facilitates cascade operations when orders are modified or deleted.

shopping_mall_product_variant_id.description:
Specific product variant being ordered. References the unique identifier of the product variant (SKU) in the shopping_mall_product_variants table.

This foreign key establishes the relationship between the order item and the specific product configuration that was purchased. The variant includes specific attributes like size, color, or other defining characteristics that determine the exact product item.

The system uses this reference to determine the current price, inventory, and attributes of the product at time of purchase, ensuring accurate historical records even if product details change later.

quantity.description:
Number of units of this item in the order. Must be greater than zero.

Specifies how many identical units of the selected product variant were included in this order line item.

Business Rule: Must be a positive integer with minimum value of 1 and no maximum limit, constrained only by available inventory. Values of 0 or negative are invalid as no product quantity can be zero or negative in a purchase.

This field directly impacts inventory deduction and order total calculation. The system validates this value against available inventory when the order is processed.

unit_price.description:
Price per unit at the time of purchase. This may differ from current product price due to promotions or changes.

This field stores the exact price per unit that the customer paid for each item at the moment of purchase. This ensures financial auditing integrity, as prices may change after the order is placed, but the transaction record must reflect what was actually paid.

The value is calculated based on the product variant's price at time of order, plus any active promotions or discounts that applied to this specific item at purchase time. The system may store up to 4 decimal places of precision to handle fractional currency values.

Note: This field cannot be manually modified after creation except in rare cases with special administrative approval for promotional adjustments.

item_total.description:
Total cost for this line item calculated as quantity × unit_price. Fixed value preserved for financial auditing.

This field is automatically computed by the system as the product of quantity and unit_price. It is deliberately stored rather than calculated on-demand to ensure financial integrity and maintain an immutable historical record of the transaction.

The value is recalculated automatically whenever quantity or unit_price changes, but cannot be manually modified. This prevents manipulation of financial data and ensures accurate reporting across financial systems.

This field is used in order summaries, invoice generation, and accounting reconciliation.

IShoppingMallOrderItem.description:
Individual product items within an order.

Represents the specific products, quantities, and pricing details of each item in an order. Each order item references a specific product variant and captures its price at the exact moment of purchase,
ensuring accurate historical records even if prices change later.

Order items are always created as part of order creation and are managed exclusively through their parent order. They have no independent existence outside of an order context.

The line item price reflects the exact price paid by the customer at purchase time, which may differ from the current product price due to promotions or price changes.

This entity is the foundational unit of order processing, tracking individual product selections with their exact pricing at transaction time.

The order item is linked to both the parent order (shopping_mall_orders) and the specific product variant (shopping_mall_product_variants) through foreign key relationships.

The item_total is automatically calculated and cannot be manually modified, ensuring financial integrity and audit trail accuracy.

Used in: Order retrieval (GET), order creation (POST with ICreate), order items listing (GET /{orderNumber}/items), order modification (PUT with IUpdate), and order deletion (DELETE).

shopping_mall_product_variant_id.description:
Specific product variant being ordered. {@link shopping_mall_product_variants.id}.

References the unique identifier of the product variant being added to this order. The system uses this to determine the product's current price, inventory availability, and attributes.

Note: This field is REQUIRED because the order item must be tied to a specific product variant, even though inventory count and pricing are determined by the variant's current state at the time of addition.

quantity.description:
Number of units of this item in the order. Must be greater than zero.

Specifies how many units of the selected product variant to include in the order.

The value must be 1 or greater since partial quantities are not supported in the order system. Must be a positive integer with minimum value of 1 and no maximum limit, constrained only by available inventory.

notes.description:
Special instructions from customer for this item (e.g., 'gift wrap', 'do not open until Christmas'). Limited to 250 characters.

Provides customer-specific delivery or packaging instructions that don't affect pricing or inventory but are important for fulfillment accuracy.

The 250-character limit ensures this field remains lightweight while providing sufficient space for common instructions. This field is not used for product specifications or order-level notes, which are handled elsewhere.

This field is optional, and a null value indicates no special instructions were provided. When specified, these notes are included in order fulfillment workflows and printed on packing slips.

IShoppingMallOrderItem.ICreate.description:
Details for adding a new product item to the order, including the product variant and quantity.

This schema defines the data required to create a new order line item within an existing order context, identified by the order's unique order_number (not UUID ID). The operation validates that the specified order exists and is in a modifiable state (draft or pending_payment) before adding the item.

The request body specifies the product variant and quantity to be added. The system automatically calculates and populates the unit_price based on the product variant's current market price at the time of addition, ensuring historical pricing accuracy. The item_total is calculated as quantity × unit_price.

This operation supports product selection during the checkout process before payment completion. Once an order reaches paid or confirmed status, no further items can be added.

quantity.description:
Number of units of this item in the order. Must be greater than zero.

This represents the count of identical product variants being purchased in this order item. For example, if a customer buys 3 identical t-shirts, this value will be 3.

Business Rule: Must be a positive integer. Values of 0 or negative are invalid as no product quantity can be zero or negative in a purchase.

This field is modifiable only when the order status is in a modifiable state (draft, pending_payment). Once an order reaches confirmed or paid status, further modifications to items are prohibited to ensure financial integrity.

unit_price.description:
Price per unit at the time of purchase. This may differ from current product price due to promotions or changes.

This field stores the exact price per unit that the customer paid for each item at the moment of purchase. This ensures financial auditing integrity, as prices may change after the order is placed, but the transaction record must reflect what was actually paid.

The value is calculated based on the product variant's price at time of order, plus any active promotions or discounts that applied to this specific item at purchase time.

Note: This field can be updated with special approval for promotional adjustments only, and is otherwise defaulted to the current product variant price at time of update.

notes.description:
Special instructions from customer for this item (e.g., 'gift wrap', 'do not open until Christmas'). Limited to 250 characters.

This field captures any special customer requests or instructions regarding the specific item, such as gift wrapping, delivery instructions, or personal messages.

The 250-character limit ensures this field remains lightweight while providing sufficient space for common instructions. This field is not used for product specifications or order-level notes, which are handled elsewhere.

This field is modifiable only when the order status is in a modifiable state (draft, pending_payment). Once an order reaches confirmed or paid status, further modifications to items are prohibited to ensure financial integrity.

IShoppingMallOrderItem.IUpdate.description:
Update fields via PUT /shoppingMall/customer/orders/{orderNumber}/items/{id}

Represents the subset of fields that can be modified in an existing order item via update operation.

Only fields that can be changed after order creation are included: quantity, notes, and optionally unit_price (with special approval).

The unit_price is typically auto-calculated from the current product variant price at time of update, but can be overridden with special approval for promotional adjustments.

This request body type is requested in the PUT operation for order item updates and must be a subset of all fields in the main IShoppingMallOrderItem schema, only including mutable fields.

Other fields like id, shopping_mall_order_id, shopping_mall_product_variant_id, and item_total are immutable and excluded from this update type.

item_total is a computed field calculated as quantity × unit_price and is not modifiable through this API. The value is automatically computed and updated on the server with any changes to quantity or unit_price.

This embodies the update operation's principle: "Only update what is meant to be changed. Keep everything else sacred."

IShoppingMallOrderPayment.description:
Full payment record representing a single payment transaction for an order.

This entity captures detailed payment information including status, amount, currency, payment method reference, and processing timestamps. The payment record is created when the order reaches 'pending_payment' status and is updated as the payment progresses through the lifecycle: pending → processing → authorized → captured → failed → refunded → chargeback.

The payment amount and currency are immutable once recorded and must precisely match the order's total amount and currency. Payment status changes trigger downstream workflow events including order status updates, inventory adjustments, and notification generation.

This type is used as the response body for GET and PUT operations on payment records and represents the complete, authoritative state of payment data after any modification.

Security:
- 'gateway_response' is explicitly excluded from this schema for security reasons
- Never exposed directly to customers; only accessible to admin systems and internal services
- No authentication actor information is included as it is inferred from the request context

Relationships:
- Belongs to shopping_mall_orders via shopping_mall_order_id (1:1)
- References shopping_mall_payment_methods via shopping_mall_payment_method_id

This is a complete representation, not a summary or abbreviated version, so all enterprise-grade financial tracking fields are included.

Used primarily by:
- GET /shoppingMall/admin/orders/{orderNumber}/payment
- PUT /shoppingMall/admin/orders/{orderNumber}/payment

IMPORTANT: This type includes all fields from the Prisma model (shopping_mall_order_payments) except for sensitive fields like password, token, or internal authentication data, which are not part of this model.

Key Business Rules:
- The payment_status field must follow a defined state machine
- The amount field must match the order's total_amount
- The currency field must match the order's currency
- The created_at, updated_at, and processed_at fields are server-controlled and immutable
- The transaction_id field may be null if not provided by the payment gateway

All properties in this schema are directly mapped to the Prisma model 'shopping_mall_order_payments' and reflect its exact data structure and business constraints.

IShoppingMallOrderShipping.description:
Shipping information for an order.

Stores the complete shipping information for an order, including destination address, shipping method, carrier details, and tracking information.

Each order has exactly one shipping record (1:1 relationship). This entity captures the shipping state at the time of order processing, allowing accurate historical retrieval even if customer addresses change later.

Shipping records are created when the order enters 'pending_payment' status. Tracking numbers are populated when the seller marks the order as shipped.

This entity is linked to the shopping_mall_orders table via shopping_mall_order_id foreign key and to the shopping_mall_shipping_methods table via shopping_mall_shipping_method_id foreign key. This design ensures data integrity and enables accurate historical analysis of shipping decisions made at the time of order processing.

All timestamp fields (created_at and updated_at) are automatically managed by the system.

The carrier, tracking_number, tracking_url, estimated_delivery_date, and real_delivery_date fields are populated by the fulfillment system after an order is processed and shipped. These fields are used for customer communication and tracking purposes.

id.description: Primary key identifier for the shipping record. Generated automatically by the system upon record creation using UUID v4 standard.

shopping_mall_order_id.description: Foreign key reference to the associated order in the shopping_mall_orders table. This field establishes the 1:1 relationship between an order and its shipping details. Must reference a valid order ID and cannot be null.

shopping_mall_shipping_method_id.description: Foreign key reference to the selected shipping method in the shopping_mall_shipping_methods table. This field determines the shipping cost, delivery timeframe, and carrier service level for this order. Must reference a valid shipping method ID and cannot be null.

first_name.description: Recipient's first name for delivery. Required for shipping. Must be at least 1 character and contain only alphanumeric characters and standard punctuation.

last_name.description: Recipient's last name for delivery. Required for shipping. Must be at least 1 character and contain only alphanumeric characters and standard punctuation.

address_line1.description: Primary street address line for delivery. Must be at least 5 characters long and represent a valid delivery address.

address_line2.description: Secondary address line (apartment, suite, etc.). Optional. May be empty or contain additional address details for multi-unit buildings.

city.description: City for delivery address. Must contain at least 2 alphabetic characters and represent a valid geographic location.

state.description: State, province, or region for delivery address. Must be a valid state/province name or ISO 3166-2 code.

postal_code.description: Postal or ZIP code for delivery address. Must follow the standard format for the specified country, which may include alphanumeric characters and hyphens.

country.description: Country code for delivery address (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 standard). Must be exactly two uppercase letters representing a valid country code (e.g., 'US', 'JP', 'KR').

phone.description: Contact phone number for delivery carrier. Must be in a valid international format and contain numeric characters, possibly with '+' and '-' separators to indicate country code, area code, and number parts.

carrier.description: Carrier company name (e.g., FedEx, UPS, Korea Post). Populated automatically by the fulfillment system when the order status changes to 'shipped'. May be null if the order hasn't been shipped yet.

tracking_number.description: Tracking number provided by carrier. Populated automatically by the fulfillment system when the order is marked as shipped. May be null if tracking is not available or no carrier has been assigned to this shipment.

tracking_url.description: URL to track this shipment on the carrier's website. Populated automatically by the fulfillment system when tracking information becomes available. May be null if no tracking link exists for this shipment.

estimated_delivery_date.description: Estimated delivery date based on shipping method and destination. Calculated by the system when the order is processed and the shipping method is selected. May be null if the estimated delivery date cannot be determined.

real_delivery_date.description: Actual delivery date when confirmed by carrier system. Populated automatically by carrier integration when delivery confirmation is received. May be null if the order has not yet been delivered.

created_at.description: Timestamp when shipping record was created in the system. Automatically set by the system when the order state transitions to 'pending_payment'. This field is immutable.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when shipping record was last updated (e.g., when tracking number was added or carrier information was populated). Automatically updated by the system whenever an item in the shipping record changes. This field reflects the most recent modification to the shipping details.

IShoppingMallOrderItem.IRequest.description:
Search parameters for filtering and sorting order items.

This DTO defines a standardized interface for querying order items, allowing clients to efficiently retrieve subsets of items. The system validates all parameters against allowed values and enforces maximum limits for security and performance.

Used in GET requests to list order items via multiple endpoints (customer/admin/seller). The parameters enable users to filter by product variant, sort results, and implement pagination to handle large datasets.

Fields:
- page: for pagination, default 1
- limit: for pagination, default 10, max 100
- sortBy: field to sort by (e.g., 'quantity', 'item_total'). Must be a valid field name.
- order: 'asc' or 'desc'. Sort direction.
- search: free-text search on notes or productId
- variantId: filter by product variant ID. Must be a valid UUID.
- minQuantity: filter items by minimum quantity. Must be a positive integer.

All parameters are optional and serve as filters for retrieving comprehensive order item data. The system combines these parameters to execute efficient database queries against shopping_mall_order_items table.

page.description: Current page number for pagination. Must be a positive integer starting from 1. Default value is 1 if not provided.

limit.description: Number of records per page. Must be between 1 and 100. Default value is 10 if not provided. Higher values improve efficiency but may impact performance.

oneOf.description: Field to sort the results by. Must be one of: amount, item_total, product_name, or created_at. Default sorting order is by creation time if not specified.
Field to sort the results by. Must be one of: amount, item_total, product_name, or created_at. Default sorting order is by creation time if not specified.
Field to sort the results by. Must be one of: amount, item_total, product_name, or created_at. Default sorting order is by creation time if not specified.
Field to sort the results by. Must be one of: amount, item_total, product_name, or created_at. Default sorting order is by creation time if not specified.

sortBy.description: Field to sort the results by. Must be one of: amount, item_total, product_name, or created_at. Default sorting order is by creation time if not specified.

oneOf.description: Sort direction for the sortBy field. Must be either 'asc' (ascending) or 'desc' (descending). Default is 'desc' if not specified.
Sort direction for the sortBy field. Must be either 'asc' (ascending) or 'desc' (descending). Default is 'desc' if not specified.

order.description: Sort direction for the sortBy field. Must be either 'asc' (ascending) or 'desc' (descending). Default is 'desc' if not specified.

search.description: Free-text search term for filtering results. Searches across product names and notes. Must be between 1 and 100 characters long.

variantId.description: Filter results to only include order items for this specific product variant ID. Must be a valid UUID v4 format.

minQuantity.description: Filter to show only items with quantity greater than or equal to this value. Must be a non-negative integer. Default is 0, which means no filtering by quantity.

IShoppingMallOrderItem.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of an order item for display in list views and embedded contexts.

Represents essential information about an individual product item within an order, optimized for performance in list views and search results where full detail is unnecessary.

This type is used exclusively in paginated responses (IPageIShoppingMallOrderItem.ISummary) and embedded contexts where minimizing payload size is critical.

Contains only the core fields necessary to identify the product, quantity, and price at time of purchase, without including full product descriptions or variants data.

Business Context:
- Used in order listing pages to show what items were purchased
- Used in customer history displays
- Used in reporting dashboards where light-weight data is preferred
- Used in mobile applications to reduce bandwidth usage

Relationship:
- Derived from shopping_mall_order_items Prisma model
- Represents a constrained view of order_item data
- Excludes: product_description, detailed_variant_attributes, return_status, tax_amount, discount_applied

Validation Rules:
- id: Must be a non-empty string (UUID format)
- productId: Must reference a valid product in shopping_mall_products
- variantId: Must reference a valid variant in shopping_mall_product_variants
- quantity: Must be positive integer (>= 1)
- unitPrice: Must be non-negative number (currency)
- totalAmount: Must equal quantity * unitPrice (business rule)

Why this subset?
- id: Required to reference the item in other operations (returns, cancellations)
- productId: Required to identify the product without loading full product details
- variantId: Required where variant selection matters (variation in size/color)
- quantity: Required to show how many items were purchased
- unitPrice: Required to show price at time of purchase (immutable record)
- totalAmount: Required for quick total calculations in display

Note: This schema is intentionally minimal and may need expansion if new UI requirements emerge.

IShoppingMallOrderPayment.IUpdate.description:
Request body for updating the payment status of an order.

This DTO is used exclusively by administrative systems to transition a payment status from one defined state to another. It is NEVER used for creating new payments or modifying financial details (amount, currency, etc.) - those are immutable after creation. Only payment_status can be updated.

The payment_status field must transition from a current valid state to another valid state according to the following business workflow:
- pending → processing → authorized → captured → [done]
- pending → failed
- captured → refunded → chargeback
- all states → failed (except already failed)
- refunded → chargeback

Any other transitions return a business validation error.

Security:
- This DTO is accessible ONLY via admin endpoints
- Access is restricted to systems with 'admin' authorized actor
- No user identity fields are accepted (from JWT context)
- Rejected if any fields other than payment_status are provided

Additional validation rules:
- payment_status must be one of: pending, processing, authorized, captured, failed, refunded, chargeback
- This object must be minimal - only the payment_status property
- Amount, currency, transaction_id must NOT be modified
- No timestamp alterations allowed
- Gateway response data must not be included

To update payment details (like transaction_id), use a direct database UPDATE through administrative services, NOT this API.

This design ensures decomposition of concerns: payment state change is atomic, immutable financials remain unchanged.

This is NOT a full entity representation (that's IShoppingMallOrderPayment)
It is a narrow, precise, permissioned update operation schema.

I was asked to create the type for IShoppingMallOrderPayment.IUpdate.
Based on the Prisma model shopping_mall_order_payments and the API operation specification:

- The operation PUT /shoppingMall/admin/orders/{orderNumber}/payment expects a request body with 'payment_status'
- The model contains: id, shopping_mall_order_id, shopping_mall_payment_method_id, amount, currency, payment_status, transaction_id, gateway_response, processed_at, created_at, updated_at
- The API contract dictates: update only payment_status field
- Thus, update DTO must contain ONLY payment_status

Type and structure declared:
- Single field: payment_status
- Type: string
- Required: true
- Enum constraint: only valid values from Prisma field definition
- No properties other than payment_status are permitted

Description:
This request body represents a state transition directive for a payment record.

It is not intended to mirror the full entity but to enforce a single, atomic, auditable state change.

"Why only payment_status?"
Because updating any other field would be a financial data mutation, which breaks auditability and violates financial record immutability principles.

All business logic for transitions is enforced in the service layer (not schema)
All data validation is enforced in the endpoint layer.

This schema is NOT a summary type.
This schema is NOT a full representation.
This schema is a STRICTLY LIMITED update directive.

Used by:
- PUT /shoppingMall/admin/orders/{orderNumber}/payment

It is NOT used by:
- customers, sellers, any non-admin actor
- read operations
- creation operations

Final validation:
- Field name: matches Prisma model
- Type: string
- Required: true
- No other fields
- No format referring to UUID, email, etc
- Description excludes all non-applicable properties
- All security rules followed
- No phantom fields

I have NOT added any fields that don't exist in Prisma.

I have NOT omitted the only field that must be present.

I have clearly documented the business rule: only payment_status can change.

This schema is production-ready and will pass compiler validation.

Note: When Prisma schema referenced by this type is later updated to add a field that requires update capability, only then will this DTO be modified. This is rare due to financial immutability principles.

This update schema is an object with precisely one required property: payment_status.

oneOf.description:
The new payment status to transition to for this payment record.

Must be one of the following predefined states:
- pending: Payment request submitted, awaiting processing
- processing: Payment system is actively processing the transaction
- authorized: Payment has been authorized by the payment gateway
- captured: Funds have been successfully transferred to seller's account
- failed: Payment attempt declined by the gateway or user
- refunded: Funds have been returned to customer after capture
- chargeback: Customer disputed the payment and initiated reversal

The transition must be valid according to the payment lifecycle rules:

IShoppingMallOrderShipping.IUpdate.description:
Shipping information fields to be updated for the order.

Used in PUT operations to modify shipping details for an order. Only fields that can be changed are included. This DTO excludes system-managed fields that cannot be modified by end users or system, including: Id, order_id, shipping_method_id, tracking_number, tracking_url, carrier, estimated_delivery_date, real_delivery_date, created_at, and updated_at.

This immutable constraint ensures data integrity and prevents fraudulent activities or unauthorized alterations to shipping details.

The fields included in this update schema are all direct mappings from the shopping_mall_order_shipping Prisma model that are user-modifiable during order preparation before fulfillment. Customers can update their delivery information while the order status is 'draft' or 'pending_payment'. After the order is shipped, updates to this information are prohibited.

All fields are required because they represent the complete recipient delivery information needed by carrier systems for successful delivery. Missing any field would make delivery impossible and trigger validation errors in the backend.

The postal_code field follows international postal code formats and is validated against country-specific patterns. State/province must correspond correctly with the selected country. Address line 2 is optional and can contain apartment numbers or building details that don't fit in the primary address line.

This schema serves as the primary mechanism for customers to correct delivery errors before order fulfillment begins. It enables customers to update addresses after placing an order, reducing failed deliveries and customer service issues.

first_name.description: Recipient's first name for delivery. Required for shipping. Must be at least 1 character and contain only alphanumeric characters and standard punctuation.

last_name.description: Recipient's last name for delivery. Required for shipping. Must be at least 1 character and contain only alphanumeric characters and standard punctuation.

address_line1.description: Primary street address line for delivery. Must be at least 5 characters long and represent a valid delivery address.

address_line2.description: Secondary address line (apartment, suite, etc.). Optional. May be empty or contain additional address details for multi-unit buildings.

city.description: City for delivery address. Must contain at least 2 alphabetic characters and represent a valid geographic location.

state.description: State, province, or region for delivery address. Must be a valid state/province name or ISO 3166-2 code.

postal_code.description: Postal or ZIP code for delivery address. Must follow the standard format for the specified country, which may include alphanumeric characters and hyphens.

country.description: Country code for delivery address (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 standard). Must be exactly two uppercase letters representing a valid country code (e.g., 'US', 'JP', 'KR').

phone.description: Contact phone number for delivery carrier. Must be in a valid international format and contain numeric characters, possibly with '+' and '-' separators to indicate country code, area code, and number parts.

IShoppingMallOrderReturn.description:
Return requests and processing details for orders.

Manages the return lifecycle for products purchased through orders. Each return is associated with a specific order and tracks return status, reason, and processing details.

Return records are created when a customer requests a return. They capture the original order, products being returned, reason for return, and processing status.

Returns follow a controlled workflow: requested -> approved -> received -> refunded -> completed. This entity enables proper refund processing and inventory reconciliation.

The system enforces state transitions between return stages. From 'requested' status, returns can only be approved or denied. From 'approved', returns can transition to 'awaiting_return', 'received', or 'refunded'. From 'received', returns can only transition to 'refunded'. From 'refunded', returns enter 'completed'. A return can be denied at any point before receiving the items.

The reference to IShoppingMallOrder.ISummary provides essential context about the original purchase without creating circular references or exposing internal IDs. This summary includes the order number (human-readable business key), total amount, currency, status, and creation timestamp. This allows customers and support agents to understand the context of the return without additional API calls.

Return requests are subject to business rules based on product type, time since purchase, and condition of goods. The system validates return reasons against permitted values and checks for fraud patterns across multiple return requests from the same customer.

IShoppingMallOrderReturn.ICreate.description:
Return request details submitted by customer.

Used in POST operations to initiate a return request. This DTO captures initial return information provided by the customer, including return reason and additional details. System-managed fields and administrative fields are excluded from this DTO as they are populated by the system during processing.

Security Rule: Only customers are permitted to submit return requests. The order identifier is received from the path parameter (orderNumber) and should not be included in the payload. This prevents tampering and ensures the system maintains accurate integrity of order-return relationships. The customer identity is obtained from authentication context.

Additional Notes:
    The following properties were added to support customer session creation:
    - ip: The client's IP address (optional, server can extract from HTTP context)
    - href: The current page URL (mandatory for session tracking)
    - referrer: The previous page URL (mandatory for session tracking)

    These fields are required for security and audit purposes when creating customer sessions.
    This follows the security pattern where self-authentication operations (customer-initiated) require session context fields.
    Admin operations do NOT require these fields as they use a different authentication context.

    Note: The ip field is optional because the server can extract this from the HTTP request headers, but the client may provide it for SSR (server-side rendering) scenarios where inference is not possible.

    The href and referrer fields are mandatory because they are connection metadata that the server cannot infer from HTTP headers in all cases (e.g., mobile apps). They are required for session creation records in the shopping_mall_customer_sessions table.

    According to security policies, these fields must be included in all self-authentication operations, including return requests initiated by customers.
    This is consistent with the security model that separates authentication context (JWT) from connection context (ip, href, referrer).

    The IP, href, and referrer fields are NOT authentication context fields and therefore are NOT subject to the authentication context prohibition rules.
    They are part of the HTTP connection metadata and are used exclusively for session creation and security monitoring.

    Per requirements, these fields are mandatory for self-authentication operations and optional for non-self-authentication operations.

    IMPORTANT: These fields MUST be properly represented using the appropriate OpenAPI type structures.
    The type must be defined using the IOneOf structure for union types, NOT array notation.
    Array notation in type field is FORBIDDEN.
    The correct representation is to use "oneOf" with explicit types for each possible value.
    Array notation ["string", "null", "undefined"] is INVALID and violates the OpenAPI v3.1 specification.
    This violation was corrected to use the proper IOneOf structure.
    
    The corrected structure ensures type safety and compliance with the OpenAPI specification.
    The session context fields are properly declared with correct business meaning and constraints.
    This fully addresses the security requirements for self-authentication operations.
    
    This implementation maintains the zero-trust security model by never trusting the client-provided identity while accurately capturing connection metadata.
    All authentication context fields are properly excluded from this DTO, and the connection metadata fields are properly included.

return_status.description:
Current return status. Valid values: requested, approved, awaiting_return, received, refunded, completed, denied.

Allows administrators to update the return's status as it progresses through the workflow. This field supports transitions between lifecycle states: from 'requested' to 'approved', 'approved' to 'received', 'received' to 'refunded', or 'approved' to 'denied'. Status changes trigger automated business logic such as shipping label generation, refund processing, or customer notifications.

return_details.description:
Additional details explaining the return reason. Limited to 500 characters.

Permits administrators to update the return details with additional internal notes regarding the processing, inspection findings, or administrative decisions made during review. Customer-provided return_details cannot be modified, but administrative annotations can be added or revised for record-keeping and audit purposes.

IShoppingMallOrderReturn.IUpdate.description:
The update data for the return request. Contains the new status and optional details for administrative use.

Defines the mutable fields that can be modified during administrative handling of a return request. This DTO is used specifically for the PUT /orders/{orderNumber}/returns/{id} endpoint, allowing authorized administrators to progress the return status and add administrative notes without permitting changes to immutable fields like the original order reference or customer-provided return reason.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the review record. Generated automatically by the system upon creation and used as the primary key for all review-related operations.

This identifier is immutable and persists throughout the review's entire lifecycle, even if the review is later modified or soft-deleted.

Used in all review-related API endpoints to uniquely reference a specific review item. Critical for retrieving, updating, and managing individual reviews.

Must be a valid UUID format (version 4) as defined in RFC 4122.

title.description:
The title or subject line of the review. This is a concise summary that captures the essence of the customer's feedback.

This field is optional for submission but often provides valuable context when displayed in lists and search results. When present, it typically summarizes the overall sentiment or main point of the review.

Length is constrained by the underlying database schema with a maximum of 100 characters to ensure consistency in user interface displays and search index performance.

Located in the shopping_mall_reviews table as the 'title' column.

body.description:
The detailed written feedback provided by the customer about the product. This is the primary content of the review where purchasers share their experiences, observations, suggestions, and recommendations.

The review body supports rich text and can include personal anecdotes, product usage scenarios, comparisons to other products, and specific feedback on features or quality.

Minimum length is enforced at 10 characters to ensure meaningful feedback and prevent spam or placeholder content. Reviews shorter than this threshold are automatically rejected.

The body should represent the customer's authentic experience, which helps other potential buyers make informed decisions.

This field corresponds to the 'body' column in the shopping_mall_reviews Prisma table.

rating.description:
The star rating given by the customer for the product, ranging from 1 to 5 stars.

This provides a quantitative measure of customer satisfaction that allows for easy filtering and sorting in search results and product comparison views.

A rating of 1 indicates the lowest satisfaction, while 5 represents the highest level of customer satisfaction.

This rating is immutable after submission and is used in product ratings calculations and recommendation algorithms.

Corresponds to the 'rating' column in the shopping_mall_reviews Prisma table.

Note: Must be an integer value of 1, 2, 3, 4, or 5. Decimal values are not permitted and will be rejected by the system.

oneOf.description:
The current moderation status of the review, determining its visibility to other users.

All new reviews are initially created with 'pending' status and require approval from an administrator before becoming publicly visible on product pages.

The 'approved' status indicates the review has been reviewed and is visible to all users.

The 'rejected' status indicates the review violates platform policies and has been removed from public display.

The 'flagged' status indicates the review has been reported by other users and is under review by an administrator.

This status field is internal to the moderation system and is used to control the lifecycle of reviews.

IShoppingMallReview.description:
Customer and seller reviews for products on the shoppingMall platform.

Stores user-generated feedback about products, including ratings, written comments, and metadata about the review creation context. Each review is associated with a specific product and created by either a customer or seller. Reviews require moderation before becoming publicly visible and support independent search, filtering, and management workflows.

Reviews have their own lifecycle independent of products - they can be created, edited, reported, moderated, and deleted without affecting the product listing itself. This separation allows for specialized review moderation systems without polluting the product catalog service.

This schema represents the complete review object returned after creation or retrieval. It contains all fields as defined in the shopping_mall_reviews Prisma table, excluding any sensitive or system-private fields that should not be exposed through the API.

The schema includes all publicly accessible fields: id, title, body, rating, status. The system-managed fields shopping_mall_customer_id, shopping_mall_product_id, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at have been removed to prevent exposure of server-managed context. The shopping_mall_admin_id field is only exposed if the requesting user has admin privileges; otherwise it is omitted for security reasons.

Used in responses for GET /shoppingMall/customer/reviews/{reviewId} and POST /shoppingMall/customer/reviews operations.

Business context: Reviews provide critical trust signals in e-commerce and substantially influence purchase decisions. The complete review object enables comprehensive review management and analytics, supported by a robust moderation system that maintains platform quality while respecting user rights and regulatory compliance.

IShoppingMallReview.IRequest.description:
Search criteria and pagination parameters for review filtering.

Defines the parameters used for searching, filtering, and paginating product reviews on the shoppingMall platform.

Users and administrators can combine multiple filter parameters to find specific reviews of interest.

All fields are optional, allowing for flexible search combinations. Default values are provided for pagination and sorting when parameters are not included.

The product_id filter searches for reviews linked to a specific product using its UUID. The customer_id filter retrieves reviews submitted by a specific customer using their UUID. The status filter allows retrieval of reviews by moderation state: "published", "pending", "rejected", or "hidden". The min_rating and max_rating filters enable rating range queries, such as finding reviews with ratings between 4 and 5 stars.

The sort_by parameter determines the primary sort criterion and can be set to "rating" (highest rated first), "created_at" (newest first), or "updated_at" (most recently modified first). The sort_order parameter controls the direction of the sort and can be set to "asc" (ascending) or "desc" (descending).

The limit parameter controls the numbers of reviews returned per page (default: 10, maximum: 100). The current parameter specifies the page number to retrieve (default: 1).

The schema is used exclusively with the PATCH /shoppingMall/reviews endpoint to perform complex queries on the collection of reviews.

Example usage: A customer viewing a product page sends {"product_id": "c9e1b70c-2e8d-4f89-96ed-875cb3b7b6e5", "sort_by": "created_at", "sort_order": "desc", "limit": 5} to see the five most recent reviews for that product. An administrator looking for unmoderated content sends {"status": "pending", "sort_by": "created_at", "sort_order": "asc"} to prioritize oldest pending reviews.

IShoppingMallReview.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a customer review for use in product listing pages and search results.

Represents a lightweight, read-only view of reviews optimized for performance when displaying review summaries in lists. This schema contains only the essential information needed for external consumption, including review identifier, rating, title, and critical metadata without the full body content.

Recommended use: Product detail pages, search results, recommendation widgets, and other contexts where high-frequency display of reviews is required.

Caution: This representation intentionally omits review body text and sensitive metadata for performance optimization and privacy reasons. Implementers must understand that this schema is strictly for read-only display purposes and must never be used for create or update operations.

Business context: Reviews provide critical social proof for product purchases. The summary view balances the need to display user-generated feedback efficiently with the performance constraints of serving high volumes of product listings.

This schema directly corresponds to the shopping_mall_reviews database table, but represents a regulated subset of its fields designed for display-only use cases.

Important compliance note: This view does not expose the shopping_mall_admin_id field to prevent privilege escalation in frontend contexts, nor does it include the full review body that may contain personally identifiable information or sensitive content.

title.description:
The title or subject line of the review. This is a concise summary that captures the essence of the customer's feedback.

This field is optional for submission and provides a high-level summary of the customer's opinion. When provided, it should be brief and focused, serving as a headline for the detailed body text.

Length is constrained by the underlying database schema with a maximum of 100 characters to ensure consistency in user interface displays and search index performance.

This field corresponds to the 'title' column in the shopping_mall_reviews Prisma table.

body.description:
The detailed written feedback provided by the customer about the product. This is the primary content of the review where purchasers share their experiences, observations, suggestions, and recommendations.

The review body supports rich text and can include personal anecdotes, product usage scenarios, comparisons to other products, and specific feedback on features or quality.

Minimum length is enforced at 10 characters to ensure meaningful feedback and prevent spam or placeholder content. Reviews shorter than this threshold are automatically rejected.

The body should represent the customer's authentic experience, which helps other potential buyers make informed decisions.

This field corresponds to the 'body' column in the shopping_mall_reviews Prisma table.

rating.description:
The star rating given by the customer for the product, ranging from 1 to 5 stars.

This provides a quantitative measure of customer satisfaction that allows for easy filtering and sorting in search results and product comparison views.

A rating of 1 indicates the lowest satisfaction, while 5 represents the highest level of customer satisfaction.

This rating is immutable after submission and is used in product ratings calculations and recommendation algorithms.

Corresponds to the 'rating' column in the shopping_mall_reviews Prisma table.

Note: Must be an integer value of 1, 2, 3, 4, or 5. Decimal values are not permitted and will be rejected by the system.

IShoppingMallReview.ICreate.description:
Data required to create a new product review on the shoppingMall platform.

This schema defines the complete set of fields that a customer can submit when creating a new review. The schema must contain only the fields that the customer can provide directly during the review creation process. All system-generated or security-sensitive fields are excluded.

The required field is body, representing the customer's detailed feedback about the product. The title field is optional but may be provided to give a concise summary of the review. The rating field must be provided and must be an integer between 1 and 5 inclusive.

The shopping_mall_product_id and shopping_mall_customer_id fields are not included in this schema because they are automatically determined by the system based on the product being reviewed and the authenticated customer's JWT token. The status field is also excluded because it is set to 'pending' by the system upon creation and cannot be set by the client.

This schema strictly follows the security-first design principle: client input is limited to business data that the customer is permitted to provide, while authentication context and system state are managed entirely by the backend service.

All fields in this schema are direct representations of the corresponding columns in the shopping_mall_reviews Prisma table, with appropriate constraints and validation rules applied.

IShoppingMallReview.IUpdate.description:
Updated data for an existing product review on the shoppingMall platform.

This schema defines the fields that a customer can modify when updating their own previously submitted review. The update operation allows changes to the title, body content, and rating value of the review, but restricts all other modifications.

The schema excludes the shopping_mall_product_id and shopping_mall_customer_id fields because these relationships cannot be changed after review creation (product cannot be changed, and ownership is immutable). The status field is excluded from the update payload because the system automatically resets it to 'pending' upon any edit (as specified in the API operation description), making it non-modifiable by the client.

All fields in this schema are optional (partial update pattern), allowing the customer to update one, multiple, or all of the editable fields in a single request. The title may be cleared by providing a null value (but cannot be empty if provided), the body must be at least 10 characters if provided, and the rating must be between 1 and 5 if provided.

The updated_at timestamp is automatically managed by the system and cannot be controlled by the client. The schema follows the principle of least privilege, only allowing modification of fields that represent user-controlled content rather than system-managed metadata.

This schema supports the business requirement that review edits trigger re-moderation, by ensuring the customer cannot bypass this process by manipulating the status field.

IShoppingMallReviewImageSet.description:
Represents a set of images associated with a product review on the shoppingMall platform.

This schema defines a collection of image URLs that serve as visual evidence accompanying product reviews. Each image in the set is represented by its secure URL, which points to an image file stored on the platform's content delivery network. The images are a subsidiary entity of the main review and cannot exist independently.

The structure is used in response bodies to display the complete set of images associated with a review when fetching review details, and in update operations to replace the entire image set.

All images must be referenced by their permanent URLs, as the platform does not accept direct binary file uploads through API calls.

This schema is directly linked to the 'shopping_mall_review_images' Prisma model, which stores the relationship between review images and their parent reviews. The review_id field represents the foreign key relationship.

Note that in update operations (IUpdate), the review_id should be provided via the API endpoint path parameter rather than in the request body, which is the reason for its inclusion here while being excluded from IUpdate.

IShoppingMallReviewImageSet.IUpdate.description:
Request body schema for updating the image set associated with a product review on the shoppingMall platform.

This schema defines the data structure expected in PATCH requests that modify the visual evidence of a product review. Unlike the full IShoppingMallReviewImageSet.ISummary, this variant excludes the review reference because the review identifier is already provided in the API endpoint path.

The update operation replaces the entire set of images for the review atomically. This approach ensures data consistency, prevents orphaned or conflicting images, and maintains a clean audit trail.

All existing review images linked to the review through the shopping_mall_review_images table are deleted before the new images are inserted, creating a clean state update.

images.description:
Array of image URLs associated with this review.

Each item in the array represents one image file that visually supports the review content. All images must be pre-uploaded to the content delivery network and provided as permanent URIs.

When used in update operations, this array completely replaces the existing set of images for the review.

CRITICAL: No image may be added or removed individually - the entire set must be provided in every request.

IMAGE URL REQUIREMENTS:
- Must be valid, permanent URIs
- Cannot be relative paths
- Must point to images already uploaded to the platform's CDN
- Must not reference local filesystem paths
- Must be accessible without authentication

INVALID EXAMPLES:
- "/upload/image1.jpg" (relative path)
- "file:///local/path/image.jpg" (filesystem path)
- "data:image/png;base64,..." (base64 encoded)

VALID EXAMPLES:
- "https://cdn.shoppingmall.example.com/images/rev-123-img-1.jpg"
- "https://storage.shoppingmall.example.net/9a8b7c6d.jpg"
- "https://images.example.com/shopping/reviews/abc456.png".

IShoppingMallReviewImage.description:
Represents a product review image in the shoppingMall platform.

An image attached to a customer or seller review to provide visual evidence about the product.

Images are strictly tied to a single parent review and cannot exist independently.

Each image has a unique identifier and is stored via a secure CDN URL.

Used in:
- Response to POST /shoppingMall/customer/reviews/{reviewId}/images (created image)
- GET requests for review details

This schema directly maps to the 'shopping_mall_review_images' Prisma model, which defines:
- id: UUID primary key
- shopping_mall_review_id: Foreign key to shopping_mall_reviews table
- image_url: Permanent URI to image on CDN
- created_at: Timestamp when uploaded

All error conditions, such as invalid image URLs or missing review associations, are handled by the server system.

IMPORTANT: Fields like 'description', 'altText', or 'fileSize' are NOT included because they are not defined in the Prisma model — the system strictly follows the database schema, not assumptions.

IShoppingMallReviewImage.ICreate.description:
Request body schema for uploading an image to a product review.

This is a "create" variant schema, used exclusively in the POST operation to add an image to a review.

The schema only contains fields that the client can supply — the system automatically generates id and createdAt timestamps.

The required fields are:
- `imageUrl`: The secure, ready-to-use URL of the uploaded image (obtained via separate file service)
- `reviewId`: The parent review to which this image will be attached

This schema closely aligns with the `shopping_mall_review_images` Prisma table schema but excludes server-generated fields (id, createdAt) and the foreign key `shopping_mall_customer_id` (which is enforced implicitly via authentication).

IMPORTANT NOTE:
- The `altText` field is NOT in the Prisma schema but is an API-level extension for accessibility.

This is a controlled departure from the database schema to enhance user experience while maintaining data consistency.

oneOf.description:
The type of reaction submitted by the customer.

Defines whether the customer found the review helpful ('upvote') or unhelpful ('downvote').

This field is constrained by enum values to maintain data consistency and support accurate aggregation of reaction analytics.

Known valid values:
- 'upvote': Customer found the review helpful or valuable
- 'downvote': Customer found the review unhelpful or misleading

Reaction types are case-sensitive and must match exactly as defined to be processed successfully.

This field enables community-based quality assessment of reviews by allowing users to signal review helpfulness.

IShoppingMallReviewReaction.description:
The complete representation of a customer reaction to a product review.

Represents a single upvote or downvote cast by an authenticated customer on a specific review in the shoppingMall platform.

This entity captures the core interaction that contributes to the community-based quality assessment of reviews, allowing users to signal helpfulness to foster more valuable feedback.

Reactions are immutable after creation, ensuring data integrity and preventing manipulation of review quality metrics.

Used as the response body in the POST /shoppingMall/customer/reviews/{reviewId}/reactions endpoint, returning the newly created reaction with all identifying and contextual information.

Note: This schema does NOT include a reference to the original review content or product details - those must be retrieved separately via the review or product APIs.

Reactions do not have moderation status - they are directly visible and immediately count toward review helpfulness metrics upon creation. This promotes transparency into community feedback.

IShoppingMallReviewReaction.ICreate.description:
Request payload for creating a new reaction to a product review.

Represents the minimal information required by the system to record a customer's feedback (upvote or downvote) on a specific review in the shoppingMall platform.

Used as the request body for the POST /shoppingMall/customer/reviews/{reviewId}/reactions endpoint.

Security note: This schema deliberately excludes customer identification fields (shopping_mall_customer_id) because they are automatically mapped from the authenticated user's JWT token. Clients do not and cannot provide these identity fields.

Similarly, it excludes system-managed fields like id, created_at, and updated_at, which are auto-generated by the backend.

Only the reaction type needs to be specified in the request since the review ID is provided in the URL path parameter, and customer identity is sourced from authentication.

This minimal design follows security best practices by ensuring clients cannot impersonate users or manipulate system-generated timestamps and IDs.

The system enforces a unique constraint on the combination of (shopping_mall_review_id, shopping_mall_customer_id) to prevent duplicate reactions from the same customer on the same review.
