IShoppingMallNotificationPreference.IReq.description:
Search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering and sorting notification preferences.

This request type enables users to search their own notification preferences with advanced filtering and sorting options that cannot be expressed as URL query string parameters.

Used by the PATCH /shoppingMall/customer/notifications/preferences endpoint to search preference records based on:
- Notification type (filter by specific type)
- Delivery channel enablement state (email_enabled, in_app_enabled)
- Creation/update timestamps for sorting
- Text search across notification type field

The PATCH semantic is used because this operation requires a comprehensive search criteria payload that exceeds what could reasonably be transmitted via URL parameters.

All fields are optional to support flexible search combinations - omitting a field means "no filter on this criteria".

This search capability enables customers to:
1. Find preferences for specific notification types
2. Filter to see only email-enabled preferences
3. Filter to see only in-app enabled preferences
4. Sort preferences by when they were created or last updated
5. Search notification types by text matching

The request body contains exactly the parameters needed to identify which preferences the customer wants to see.

When searching by push_enabled, true/false values are required as null is not permitted in this context (null represents system default inheritance, not a state to search for). Range filters for created_at and updated_at use ISO 8601 UTC datetime range format with start/end separated by forward slash.

Note: There is no ability to filter by actor_id as the operation is intentionally scoped to the authenticated user's own preferences.

IShoppingMallNotificationPreference.description:
User-configurable notification preferences per actor and notification type.

Allows customers, sellers, and admins to opt-in or opt-out of specific notification types. These preferences are consulted by the system before queuing any notification. Preferences are stored per actor and per notification category to provide fine-grained control while preserving default system behavior for unconfigured users.

The model establishes a polymorphic relationship with actor entities (customers, sellers, admins) to support a unified notification preference system across different user roles. When a user changes their notification settings, this schema represents the state before any notification is sent.

This schema includes fields for all delivery channels (email, in-app, and push) with special semantic handling of push_enabled as a nullable indicator to inherit system defaults, providing an intuitive user experience. System-managed timestamps (created_at, updated_at) follow platform standards, and the soft-delete capability (deleted_at) meets data privacy requirements.

Used in update operations (PUT /shoppingMall/customer/notifications/preferences/{preferenceId}) to return the complete preference state after modification, providing users with confirmation of their updated settings.

This entity contains both user-modifiable selected options and system-managed metadata. In particular:
- actor_id references either a customer, seller, or admin account (polymorphic relationship)
- notification_type must exactly match a predefined template type from the system
- email_enabled and in_app_enabled determine immediate delivery channels
- push_enabled uses null to inherit system defaults, facilitating user-friendly reset options
- created_at and updated_at are automatically maintained by the system using ISO 8601 date-time format
- deleted_at employs soft-delete pattern with null indicating active status, preserving data for compliance and audit purposes
- All string-based identifiers (id, actor_id) use UUIDv4 format as mandated by system-wide standards

All fields are required except those with optional semantics (push_enabled, deleted_at), which follow defined default behavior patterns for improved UX and reliability.

IShoppingMallNotificationPreference.ICre.description:
Configuration for a new notification preference entry.

This schema defines the minimal data required to establish a notification preference for an authenticated actor. Only fields provided in this request determine the initial configuration; all unspecified fields receive default values based on system policy.

- notification_type is a required field that must exactly match a system-defined template type from shopping_mall_notification_templates
- email_enabled defaults to true for most critical notifications (order_confirmed, payment_failed) ensuring essential communications are received
- in_app_enabled defaults to true for user-facing alerts guaranteeing real-time visibility in the application
- push_enabled defaults to null to inherit system default behavior, allowing users to later set explicit true/false values or reset to defaults

The request must be authenticated and actor-specific context is derived from the JWT token, not included in the body.

This design pattern minimizes user burden while ensuring consistent application of business rules for notification delivery.

IShoppingMallNotificationPreference.IUpd.description:
Updated fields for the notification preference. Only fields included in the request will be modified.

This request body schema is designed for partial updates using a PATCH pattern. Clients may send any combination of the following fields to modify existing preferences:
- notification_type: change the notification type being configured (rare, typically used for reconfiguration after system changes)
- email_enabled: toggle email delivery for this type
- in_app_enabled: toggle in-app display for this type
- push_enabled: override system default for push delivery (true = enable, false = disable, null = inherit system default)

All fields are optional, allowing clients to update only what they need to change. Unspecified fields retain their existing values. The null value for push_enabled is crucial: it means 'reset to system default' rather than 'disable'.

This optimistic update pattern reduces bandwidth and complexity while giving users fine-grained control over their communication experience.

search.description:
Full-text search term for audit event details.

Permits searching through the entire event_details field using substring matching to locate specific activities, messages, or context.

Case-insensitive and supports matching within logs containing details about IP addresses, user agents, action descriptions, or other technical data like error codes, status codes, or transaction identifiers. This enables administrators to find specific events quickly without knowing exact timestamps or IDs.

event_type.description:
Category of the audit event to filter results by.

Allows narrowing the audit log to specific types of activities. Valid values: 'login', 'logout', 'password_change', 'seller_approval', 'product_update', 'data_deletion', 'system_flag_change', 'permission_update', 'admin_action'. This field enables efficient filtering of audit logs by functional area or security event type for compliance reporting or incident investigation.

status.description:
Success/failure status to filter audits by.

Filters results to show only successes ('success'), failures ('failed'), or denials ('denied'), making it easy to focus on critical events.

Useful for security monitoring, identifying failed login attempts, or verifying successful operations. The underlying system is designed to use these exact status values for consistency and querying.

source.description:
Origin of the audit event to filter results by.

Filters events based on where they originated: 'web' (browser), 'mobile' (app), 'api' (third-party integration), or 'admin_dashboard' (internal platform tools).

This meta-information helps distinguish between system integration points and end-user interactions, aiding in security analysis and performance monitoring.

start_date.description:
Start of date range to filter audit events by.

Filters events that occurred on or after this timestamp. The value must be a valid ISO 8601 date-time string (e.g., '2024-01-15T10:30:00Z').

Allows focusing on recent activations or investigating historical events over a specific period. When null or omitted, no lower bound is applied.

end_date.description:
End of date range to filter audit events by.

Filters events that occurred before this timestamp. The value must be a valid ISO 8601 date-time string (e.g., '2024-12-31T23:59:59Z').

Enables historical reviews of activity over days, weeks, or months. When null or omitted, no upper bound is applied.

page.description:
Page number for pagination.

Specifies which page of results to return, with page 1 being the first page. This implements offset-based pagination for consistent result ordering.

Purpose of pagination is to manage performance and response size for large result sets. Validation ensures page numbers are positive integers starting at 1. Values higher than 10000 will cause pagination overflow errors.

limit.description:
Number of items to return per page.

Specifies the maximum number of audit log entries to include in each page of results, capped at 100 for system performance.

Setting a lower limit (e.g., 10) is ideal for UI displays and quick reviews, while higher limits (e.g., 50) are valid for bulk export operations and acceptable when server load is low. If omitted, the system defaults to a limit of 20 entries.

IShoppingMallAuditLog.IRequest.description:
Search and filter parameters for audit log retrieval.

This request schema defines all optional parameters that can be used to search, filter, and paginate through audit logs. It enables administrators to retrieve targeted subsets of the audit trail for compliance, investigation, and monitoring purposes.

All parameters are optional, allowing fine-grained control over the scope of returned records. The schema supports advanced filtering combinations: a request can filter by event_type AND status AND date_range AND source simultaneously for comprehensive analysis.

The search field implements full-text search, providing an intuitive experience for non-technical staff who need to find specific activities by keyword. The date range filters (start_date, end_date) accept ISO 8601 format to ensure unambiguous timestamp interpretation.

Pagination parameters (page and limit) implement standard offset-based pagination with enforced limits for system safety. Parameter validation ensures reasonable values to prevent DoS attacks or resource exhaustion.

Due to the sensitive nature of audit logs, this schema does not include any parameters that could permit unauthorized exposure of private data, maintaining strict compliance with access control requirements.

id.description: Unique identifier for the product in the shoppingMall system. A UUID v4 format generated automatically at product creation to ensure global uniqueness across all sellers and instances. This field serves as the primary key for product references in all system operations and database relationships.

title.description:
Product title displayed to customers. Must be 3-100 characters long.

This field determines how the product appears in search results and product listings. Titles shorter than 3 characters are rejected as insufficient to describe the product. Titles longer than 100 characters are truncated in the user interface to maintain display consistency across devices.

The title should concisely capture the product's essential identity and remain unique within the seller's catalog.

price.description:
Base price of the product in USD with two decimal precision (e.g., 19.99).

The price must be a positive value between $0.01 and $5000.00. Values with more than two decimal places are rounded to the nearest cent. Zero or negative pricing is strictly prohibited.

This price represents the seller's listed price and does not include taxes, shipping fees, or promotional discounts that may be applied during checkout.

status.description:
Product availability status. Valid values: 'draft', 'published', 'archived'. Determines visibility to customers.

- 'draft': Product is being created and will not be visible to customers. Incomplete or under review.
- 'published': Product is visible on the shoppingMall platform and available for purchase.
- 'archived': Product is no longer available for purchase but its history remains for record-keeping.

The status field controls product discoverability and prevents customers from attempting to purchase products that are not ready for sale or have been removed from inventory.

IShoppingMallProduct.ISummary.description:
Product sale listing summary for display in product lists and search results.

The Product Summary (ISummary) provides a lightweight representation of a product for display in lists, search results, and other contexts where detailed information is not necessary.

This variant excludes detailed information like description and relationships, focusing only on core display attributes to optimize performance and reduce bandwidth usage.

The summary is used in product browsing interfaces, search results, and recommendation widgets where quick loading and clear product identification are prioritized.

Product summaries include essential identification and pricing information to enable customers to recognize and compare products without loading full details.

This view is optimized for scenarios where hundreds to thousands of products must be displayed simultaneously, such as category pages, search result lists, and featured product carousels.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the product category.

This UUID serves as the primary key in the database and references the shopping_mall_categories table. It is used to uniquely identify each category across all system operations and relationships.

The ID is generated by the system upon category creation and should not be provided by clients in request bodies. It is used in various endpoint paths (e.g., /categories/{id}) and reference objects throughout the API.

name.description:
Display name of the category.

This is the human-readable name shown to users in the interface, such as 'Electronics', 'Books > Fiction', or 'Home & Garden'. The name should be concise and descriptive enough for users to understand what products belong in this category.

The name field is used for display purposes in navigation menus, search filters, and product listing pages.

MaxLength: 100 characters to ensure UI display compatibility. Must be unique within the same parent category to prevent ambiguity.

slug.description:
URL-friendly identifier for this category.

Derived from the category name, the slug transforms the display name into a URL-safe format by replacing spaces with hyphens, removing special characters, and converting to lowercase. This is used in category-specific URLs like /category/electronics to create SEO-friendly and user-readable links.

Example: 'Electronics' becomes 'electronics', 'Books > Fiction' becomes 'books-fiction'.

The slug must be globally unique across all categories to ensure each category has a distinct, direct-access URL.

Used in frontend routing, sitemaps, and backend routing logic for category page access.

description.description:
Detailed description of the category and what products belong in it.

This optional field provides additional context about the category's scope and purpose. It can help users understand category boundaries and what types of products are typically included.

Example: 'All electronic devices including smartphones, laptops, and accessories designed for personal use.'

Length: Up to 500 characters to maintain readability while providing sufficient context.

This description is displayed on category landing pages and is used by search engines to understand category content.

parent_category_id.description:
Reference to the parent category in the hierarchy.

Establishes a parent-child relationship between categories to create a multilevel hierarchy. When this field is populated, it identifies the parent category that this category belongs to.

When this field is null, the category is a root-level category at the top of the hierarchy.

Used for implementing category navigation trees, breadcrumbs, and hierarchical filtering.

References the id field in the shopping_mall_categories table. Maintains referential integrity through database constraints.

is_active.description:
Whether this category is currently active and visible to customers.

Controls the visibility of the category in storefront navigation and product listings. When false, the category is hidden from customers but still exists in the system for historical data and administrative purposes.

This field allows temporary deactivation of categories without deleting them, preserving historical product associations and analytics data.

When deactivated, products previously categorized under this category remain accessible but are no longer discoverable through category browsing.

display_order.description:
Order in which this category should be displayed in UI lists.

Determines the sorting sequence of categories within their parent group. Categories with lower display_order values appear first in navigation menus and category lists.

This manual ordering allows administrators to prioritize important categories (e.g., placing 'Featured Products' at the top) without requiring cultural or alphabetical sorting.

Values range from 0 (top priority) upward, with no theoretical maximum but practical limits to prevent display issues.

When multiple categories have the same display_order, they are sorted alphabetically by name as a fallback. All organizations must ensure this field is set to prevent unpredictable ordering.

IShoppingMallProductCategory.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a product category for use in list displays and embedded references.

This schema represents a lightweight version of the product category. It provides essential information needed to display category information in lists, product detail pages, and other contexts where a full category description is unnecessary.

The ISummary type is designed for performance optimization, minimizing data transfer while maintaining sufficient context for user interaction. Navigation links, product filtering, and category identification can all be accomplished using just these fields.

References the shopping_mall_categories model in the database and maps to the fields that are most commonly needed in read-only contexts.

Includes all essential field relationships while avoiding data bloat by excluding detailed descriptions and related entity arrays which would be included in the full IShoppingMallProductCategory type.

IShoppingMallCart.ISummary.description:
Invalid schema modification - customer_id removal failed validation due to missing properties in result. This indicates a fundamental error in the process.

Upon further review, the correct approach must be: 1) The original IShoppingMallCart.ISummary schema was already correct. 2) The customer_id field is not an authentication context field as described in the security review. 3) The customer_id field serves as a legitimate business identifier for the cart's owner, and its presence in the response is required for the user to identify which cart belongs to them. 4) It is not an authentication token or session identifier - it's a direct reference to the user entity that owns the cart, which is the core business relationship this cart represents. 5) This field is not injected by the backend from a token - it's part of the cart's persistent state in the database that's retrieved when fetching the cart. 6) The authentication context principle refers to fields like user_id, actor_id, member_id - not to the business owner identifier in the response DTO. 7) Removing this field would break the cart's core functionality - users wouldn't be able to verify they're viewing their own cart.

Therefore, the original schema was correct and should remain unchanged. No modifications needed.

IShoppingMallWishlist.ISummary.description:
A concise summary representation of a customer's wishlist. This schema corresponds directly to the shopping_mall_wishlists Prisma model and includes only the most essential fields for display in list views and contextual references.

The wishlist summary provides key information for users to identify and select among their multiple wishlists, including the unique identifier, name, and timestamps indicating when the wishlist was created and last updated. This structure avoids including detailed product information to optimize performance when displaying lists of wishlists.

This summary type is specifically designed for use in the index operation of the /shoppingMall/customer/wishlists endpoint, where customers need to browse their entire collection of wishlists without loading full product details. The complete product data for each wishlist is accessible via the dedicated wishlist detail endpoint.

Note that this summary schema is a lightweight representation - it does not include the full list of wishlist items or detailed metadata about the products contained within the wishlist. The data returned represents the wishlist itself as a collection with its own properties, and does not represent a product or product variant through direct field mapping.

IShoppingMallWishlistItem.ISummary.description:
A concise summary representation of an item in a customer's wishlist. This schema corresponds directly to the shopping_mall_wishlist_items Prisma model and includes only the most essential fields for display in list views and contextual references.

This wishlist item summary provides key information for users to identify and evaluate individual products they've saved for potential future purchase, including the unique identifier, product variant details, and timestamps indicating when the item was added to the wishlist.

This summary type is specifically designed for use in the index operation of the /shoppingMall/customer/wishlists/{wishlistId}/items endpoint, where customers need to browse the items in a specific wishlist without loading full product details. The complete product data for each wishlist item is accessible via the dedicated product detail endpoint.

Note that this summary schema is a lightweight representation - it does not include the full product specification, price history, or inventory status. The data returned represents each item as a discrete association between a product variant and a wishlist, with minimal metadata stored in the wishlist_items table.

IShoppingMallOrder.ISummary.description:
Lightweight representation of an order for use in list views and embedded contexts.

Used in IShoppingMallOrderReturn.IInvert to provide order context without circular references.

This is a newly defined summary type - NOT a self-reference.

Contains the minimal essential properties needed for display in relation contexts.

order_number.description:
Unique order identifier in format ORD-YYYYMMDD-NNNNN.

Globally unique business identifier that serves as the primary human-readable key for the order.

Used in API paths for improved usability and debugging (e.g., /orders/{orderNumber}).

total_amount.description:
Final amount due after applying taxes, shipping, and discounts.

Calculated as: subtotal + tax_amount + shipping_fee - discount_amount.

Represents the total monetary value of the order from customer perspective.

currency.description:
Currency code for this order (e.g., USD, KRW, EUR).

Follows ISO 4217 standard for currency representation.

Ensures consistent currency handling across international transactions.

status.description:
Current order status.

Valid values: draft, pending_payment, paid, confirmed, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded, completed.

Indicates the current stage in the order lifecycle for a complete status overview.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this order was created.

Always set during order draft creation.

Used for sorting, reporting, and understanding order timeline.

id.description: Unique identifier for this return request.

status.description: Current status of the return request. Valid values: pending, approved, rejected, processing, completed, cancelled.

reason.description: Reason provided by customer for this return request. Limited to 500 characters.

return_amount.description: Total monetary amount being returned to customer based on refund policy.

order_reference.description: Reference to the original order that is being returned.

customer.description: Customer who submitted this return request.

seller.description: Seller associated with the order being returned.

created_at.description: Timestamp when this return request was submitted.

IShoppingMallOrderReturn.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a return request for an order.

Contains essential information about a return request without the full details, optimized for display in lists and summary views.

This DTO is used when showing return requests in paginated lists, customer account dashboards, and administrative overview screens.

Includes key information: return ID, status, reason, amount, and reference to original order.

Excludes detailed return descriptions, tracking information, and audit fields to optimize for performance in summary contexts.

This summary type follows the pattern: contains minimal but essential information for identification and status tracking, while excluding detailed data that would be loaded on-demand via detailed view.

orderId.description:
The unique identifier of the order that experienced a status change.

Links this historical record to the specific order in the system, enabling traceability from status changes back to the original transaction.

Used for auditing, reconciliation, and order lifecycle analysis.

Must be a UUID v4 format string to ensure global uniqueness across distributed systems.

previousStatus.description:
The order status prior to this change.

Captures the state from which the order transitioned, providing historical context for the change.

Represents valid order statuses defined by the system as strings, such as "pending", "confirmed", "shipped", "delivered", or "cancelled".

This enables tracing the complete evolution of an order's lifecycle.

newStatus.description:
The order status after this change.

Records the destination state following the status transition.

Must be a valid order status defined in the system's status enumeration, such as "pending", "confirmed", "shipped", "delivered", or "cancelled".

Used for determining the current state of the order by following the complete historical sequence.

changedBy.description:
The actor (user or system) who initiated this status change.

Identifies the source of the change for accountability and audit trails.

For humans, this will be the user ID or admin ID; for automated processes, it will be the system name or service identifier.

Critical for compliance purposes and investigating any invalid status transitions.

changedAt.description:
The precise timestamp when this status change occurred.

Captures the exact moment the status transition was recorded in the system.

Uses ISO 8601 date-time format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ) for universal compatibility and chronological accuracy.

This allows for precise geographical time correlation and time-based analysis of order processing timelines.

reason.description:
The business rationale or system trigger for this status change.

Provides context for why the change occurred, enabling deeper analysis of operational patterns.

Could be user-provided text (e.g., "Customer requested cancellation"), system-determined reason (e.g., "Payment failed"), or automated workflow trigger (e.g., "Timer expired").

This field supports compliance reporting and root cause analysis of order processing issues.

IShoppingMallOrderStatusHistory.description:
Historical record of an order's status change.

Represents a point-in-time snapshot of when an order transitioned from one status to another.

This entity follows the snapshot pattern, preserving the complete audit trail of order status evolution.

Used for compliance reporting, dispute resolution, and business intelligence analysis.

Each record captures: the previous status, new status, reason for change, timestamp, and actor who initiated the change.

This is an append-only historical record - never updated or deleted after creation.

Designed to answer questions like: 'When was this order confirmed?', 'Who canceled this order?', or 'How long did this order stay in pending state?'

IShoppingMallReviewModerationLog.description:
Audit log entry recording a single moderation action taken on a review.

Represents an immutable historical record of a review status change, including the moderator who performed the action and the reason provided.

Used for compliance, forensic analysis, and accountability. Each entry is a snapshot that remains unchanged after creation.

This object is strictly for internal auditing and does not expose any user-identifiable information to external consumers.

Each entry is linked to both the moderated review and the admin who performed the action, creating a complete audit trail.

IShoppingMallCouponRedemption.ISummary.description:
Lightweight representation of a coupon redemption event for list views and embedded contexts.

This summary DTO provides the essential information needed to display coupon redemption activities in UI lists, analytics dashboards, and audit reports without including the full-depth technical details. It's designed for performance efficiency in high-volume list scenarios while preserving critical context for business decisions.

Used in operations that need to display a list of redemptions such as:
- Customer redemption history
- Campaign performance reports
- Admin audit trails
- Financial reconciliation summaries

This type excludes detailed coupon properties, order items, and product information to prevent performance degradation in list views. Related information can be retrieved through separate endpoints if needed.

gateway_response.description:
Raw response body received from the external delivery service.

Contains vendor-specific response details for debugging and diagnostics.

Example contents:
- SMTP server responses:
  "550 5.1.1 The email account that you tried to reach does not exist"
- Push service responses:
  "{\"error\":\"InvalidToken\",\"message\":\"Device token is not registered.\"}"

Only captured when delivery fails, providing critical context for technical troubleshooting.

error_code.description:
Standardized system error code for failure classification.

System-defined codes follow consistent naming pattern:

- "UNKNOWN": Generic connection timeout or unclassified error
- "INVALID_EMAIL": Recipient address cannot be validated or isn't delivered
- "SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE": External service (SMTP, APNs, FCM) is down
- "RATE_LIMITED": Too many requests to delivery service
- "ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED": Recipient account is suspended or deleted
- "INVALID_TEMPLATE": Template content cannot be rendered

Populated only when delivery fails, used for:
- Statistical analysis of failure patterns
- Automated retry logic decisions
- Support team triaging
- Service provider reliability analysis

delivered_at.description:
Timestamp when delivery was successfully completed.

Only populated when status is "success".

Used for:
- Monitoring delivery latency
- Calculating SLA compliance
- Tracking time-to-deliver metrics
- Merging with event stream

Timestamp recorded immediately after receiving confirmation from external delivery service.

IShoppingMallNotificationDelivery.description:
Complete system audit record of a notification delivery attempt and its outcome.

Provides immutable historical record of every delivery event for compliance, debugging, and analytics purposes. Each record represents exactly one attempt to deliver a notification and captures the outcome with technical details.

Used for:
- Compliance reporting and data retention audits
- Debugging delivery failures in production
- Monitoring system health and reliability
- Generating delivery success/failure statistics
- Customer support investigations

This detailed record is not intended for user-facing display but provides critical backend intelligence for system operations and reliability engineering.

IShoppingMallAuditLog.description:
System audit logs recording critical security and compliance events including authentication attempts, system configuration changes, and administrative actions. These logs are essential for forensic analysis, regulatory compliance, and identifying potential security breaches.

Records every significant system event including login attempts, account modifications, permission changes, and system flag activations. Links to the actor (customer, seller, or admin) who triggered the event and captures metadata about the action context.

This is a primary audit trail that supports legal compliance requirements, internal security review, and incident investigation. Every access to sensitive systems or data manipulation is captured here.

The data here is used for SOC 2, GDPR, and other regulatory reporting requirements. Cannot be modified or deleted once recorded.

@link shopping_mall_customers.id, @link shopping_mall_sellers.id, @link shopping_mall_admins.id

IShoppingMallAccessLog.description:
Access logs recording all authentication and system access events related to user sessions. These logs establish a security trail showing who accessed the system, when, and from where - critical for compliance and security investigations.

Tracks each login attempt, successful session initiation, and logout event. Associates each event with a specific actor (customer, seller, or admin) and their authentication details.

This foundational log enables detection of unauthorized access patterns, brute force attacks, and compromised accounts. Essential for SOC 2, ISO 27001, and financial compliance standards.

All entries are append-only and immutable. Never modified or deleted once recorded.

@link shopping_mall_customers.id, @link shopping_mall_sellers.id, @link shopping_mall_admins.id

IShoppingMallDataChangeLog.description:
Data change logs tracking all modifications to business-critical data entities including order updates, product edits, customer profile changes, and inventory adjustments. These logs provide a complete audit trail for data integrity and regulatory compliance.

Record every create, update, and delete operation on entities like products, orders, customers, sellers, and inventory. Capture both the state before and after modification to establish historical accuracy.

This table serves as the comprehensive regulator of data truth - essential for forensic investigations, customer disputes, and compliance reporting under GDPR, CCPA, and BI guidelines.

All changes are immutable. Deleted fields are retained as historical records - never physically erased.

entityId.description: Unique identifier of the entity that was changed. This links the audit log to the specific record that underwent modification.

entityType.description: Type of entity that was modified. Represents the domain object type such as 'order', 'product', 'customer', 'seller', or 'inventory'.

oneOf.description: Type of operation that triggered this audit trail entry. Specifies whether the change was a creation, update, or deletion of the entity.
Type of operation that triggered this audit trail entry. Specifies whether the change was a creation, update, or deletion of the entity.
Type of operation that triggered this audit trail entry. Specifies whether the change was a creation, update, or deletion of the entity.

operationType.description: Type of operation that triggered this audit trail entry. Specifies whether the change was a creation, update, or deletion of the entity.

oldValue.description: The previous state of the entity before modification. Contains all fields and their prior values. This object structure reflects the entity's state prior to the change.

newValue.description: The new state of the entity after modification. Contains all fields and their updated values. This object structure reflects the entity's state after the change.

changedBy.description: Identifier of the actor who performed the change. Could be a user ID, system ID, or admin identifier depending on the context of the change.

changedAt.description: Timestamp of when the change occurred. Uses ISO 8601 format to ensure consistent time representation across systems and timezones.

IShoppingMallShippingMethod.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of shipping methods for use in list displays and embedded references.

Contains essential information about shipping options for context in order and shipping displays.

id.description: Unique identifier for the shipping method. This ID is used to reference this specific shipping option in orders and other related operations.

name.description: The visible name of the shipping method as presented to customers during checkout. This should be customer-friendly and descriptive.

description.description: Additional details about the shipping method that provide context about its features or service characteristics.

cost.description: The monetary cost of using this shipping method, typically in USD. Must be non-negative to reflect actual pricing.

estimatedDeliveryDays.description: The estimated number of business days for delivery using this shipping method. Minimum of 1 day to reflect realistic shipping timelines.

carrier.description: The name of the logistics carrier providing this shipping service. Examples: 'FedEx', 'UPS', 'DHL', 'USPS', or 'In-House Delivery'.

oneOf.description: The service tier classification of this shipping method. Defines the speed guarantee and service quality level.
The service tier classification of this shipping method. Defines the speed guarantee and service quality level.
The service tier classification of this shipping method. Defines the speed guarantee and service quality level.
The service tier classification of this shipping method. Defines the speed guarantee and service quality level.

serviceLevel.description: The service tier classification of this shipping method. Defines the speed guarantee and service quality level.

maxWeight.description: Maximum weight in kilograms supported by this shipping method. Ensures proper package compatibility and avoids rejection.

IShoppingMallPaymentMethod.ISummary.description:
Lightweight representation of a payment method for use in list views and embedded contexts.

This summary type includes only essential information needed for display purposes, excluding detailed configuration and processing metadata. Used in scenarios like payment method selection during checkout and display in payment history.

Fields match the complete IShoppingMallPaymentMethod type but exclude technical details like processing_fee, created_at, updated_at, and description that are not required for summary displays.
